News.title: Woman paid tribute to ‘darling’ XL Bully named Cookie after it mauled boyfriend’s dad to death in garden, court told
News.content:
DOG ATTACK Woman paid tribute to ‘darling’ XL Bully named Cookie after it mauled boyfriend’s dad to death in garden, court told

A WOMAN paid tribute to her “darling” XL Bully after it mauled her boyfriend’s dad to death in the garden, a court heard.

Keven Jones, 62, suffered severe blood loss after being bitten at least twice by the animal, which was called Cookie.



Jurors heard Chanel Fong, who allegedly owned the dog with Keven’s son Josh Jones, was inside her house in Wrexham, North Wales at the time.

The 33-year-old told police she heard him say “Cookie, get off me” after he walked into the garden.



Following the horror, which took place in May 2022 before a ban on XL Bullies was introduced, the dog was destroyed.

Caernarfon Crown Court heard Fong later wrote on Facebook: “Cookie didn’t attack Keven.



“He’s a big boy and plays too rough.”

She also allegedly said the male dog was “not aggressive in the slightest” and “just thinks he’s still a small pup”.



Fong is said to have added: “Rest in peace my darling stupid Cookie-Doe.”

Jurors heard Keven had been in “poor” health and was “addicted to Class A drugs” at the time of his death.

Prosecutor Mark Connor said he was also on a methadone prescription and taking blood thinners.



He added: “All of that was known to Chanel Fong and he had been left on his own to deal with two powerful XL bully dogs.”

The court heard Fong’s other dog – a female named Rogue – was “in season”, which could have led to issues with Cookie.

Home Office pathologist Dr Matthew Lyall said Keven weighed 10st and had drugs in his system at the time of his death.

He added: “It’s likely death would have occurred within a small number of minutes.”

Fong has denied being the owner or in charge of a dangerously out of control American XL Bully which caused injury resulting in death.



Her partner – Keven’s son – was not at the house at the time.

The trial continues.

News.title: Boy, 13, among six teens arrested after cop hit by ‘stolen car while probing burglary’ and rushed to hospital
News.content:
COP STRUCK Boy, 13, among six teens arrested after cop hit by ‘stolen car while probing burglary’ and rushed to hospital

SIX teenage boys have been arrested after a police officer was hit by a car during a suspected burglary probe.

The officer was struck as police moved to secure a suspected stolen vehicle in Sunderland yesterday morning.



Six boys aged between 13 and 17 were arrested following the incident and remain in police custody.

Northumbria Police said they received a report of a suspected burglary at an address in the Burdon area of the city at 6.45am.



A car was reported stolen and driven into the Durham Constabulary area.

The vehicle was spotted parked on Cooperative Terrace in Sunderland shortly after 8.30am.

But when an officer approached on foot and tried to secure the car, it drove away, hitting another parked vehicle and injuring him.

The officer was taken to hospital and has since been discharged.

The road remains closed to traffic, with police expected to stay at the scene for several hours.

Detective Chief Inspector Rebecca Fenney, of Northumbria Police, said: “Firstly, we’d like to extend our thoughts to the officer from our neighbouring police force who has been injured in this incident.

“Police officers attend work with the sole intention to help people – not to be hurt in the line of duty.



“We wish this officer a speedy recovery and we’d like to thank him and his colleagues for their assistance with the response to the initial report.

“Our investigation remains at an early stage, however we already have got six suspects in custody.

“We’re aware this incident will have caused concern and disruption in the local community.

“As this is a live investigation, we ask the public not to speculate on the circumstances or comment on social media.

“Officers will remain in the area, and we would ask anyone with further concerns, or information to report, including CCTV, dashcam, or mobile phone footage, to get in touch with us.”



Assistant Chief Constable Richie Allen, from Durham Constabulary, said: “Our thoughts are with the officer who sustained injuries during the incident.”

News.title: How to make a pinhole projector to watch the solar eclipse safely without glasses tonight
News.content:
THE UK is gearing up for a sensational celestial show on Wednesday, when the best solar eclipse in decades will grace our skies.

But with certified eclipse glasses selling out fast, people are looking for alternative ways to witness the phenomenon.



Even if you do manage to buy a genuine pair online, they most likely won’t arrive on time for the solar eclipse.

A Royal Observatory Greenwich spokesperson said: “We have sold out of solar eclipse glasses, both online and in our shops, due to an unprecedented volume of orders.”



How do you make a pinhole eclipse viewer?

If proper glasses are unavailable, the best way to see Wednesday’s partial solar eclipse is to make an indirect viewer instead.

All you need to do is punch a small, clean hole in one piece of card and use a second section white card as a screen in your other hand or on the floor.



You have to stand with your back to the Sun, hold the holed card above the screen and let sunlight pass through it.

The distance between the cards needs to be adjusted until a small image of the Sun appears clearly on the other white card below.

During this week’s partial eclipse, it should appear as a crescent.

Only watch the projected image – never turn around and look at the Sun through the hole.



Looking directly at the Sun may damage the retina without causing any pain.

So it is possible to cause a permanent injury without even noticing anything is wrong until it is too late.

Regular sunglasses are also unsafe for viewing a solar eclipse, no matter how much they cost or how dark they might appear.

What other ways can you watch the eclipse without glasses?

There are even simpler ways to enjoy the solar eclipse that need no assembly whatsoever.



UKHSA says “you can watch the eclipse indirectly without any specialist equipment at all”, listing safe options including “viewing the Sun’s image projected through a colander or the gaps between tree leaves”.

For the colander method you will also want a sheet of white card or paper.

Lay it on the ground or hold it out, stand with your back to the Sun and position the colander so sunlight shines through its holes onto the card.

Each hole will then project its own tiny crescent Sun.



The tree method requires nothing at all – stand under a leafy tree and look at the shadows on the ground, where the gaps between leaves act as natural pinholes.

What time will the eclipse happen in the UK?

On Wednesday, August 12, a deep partial solar eclipse will sweep across the UK.

Astronomers have said it will be the most striking eclipse Britain has seen since 1999.

Between 90% and 96% of the Sun will be covered by the Moon n the UK,.

Depending on where you are, the Moon will start to pass the Sun at around 6.15pm, with the maximum eclipse roughly an hour later between 7.05pm and 7.15pm, and the event finishing just after 8pm.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

As the eclipse occurs in the evening in the UK, the sun will be low in the western sky, so you will need a clear, unobstructed view towards the horizon.

News.title: Teacher ‘had sex with pupil up to 30 times & kissed another on lunch breaks after comparing herself to porn mag model’
News.content:
'PAEDO MISS' Teacher ‘had sex with pupil up to 30 times & kissed another on lunch breaks after comparing herself to porn mag model’

A CHEMISTRY teacher had sex with a schoolboy up to 30 times after comparing herself to a porn mag model, a court heard.

Sally-Anne Bowen is accused of abusing two boys at a North London school when they were aged 14 and 15 in the 1980s.



The teacher – then aged 25 – allegedly “engaged in flirtatious conduct” with the pupils and “engaged in sexual relationships with them both”.

Jurors heard Bowen had sex with the first boy between 20 and 30 times and he believed they were in a relationship.



She allegedly let the second boy touch her breasts and kiss her during lunch at a cafe near the school.

Prosecutor Madeleine Wolfe said: “The prosecution case is that when Ms Bowen worked at the school, that she engaged in flirtatious conduct towards these two boys and she encouraged and engaged in sexual relationships with them both and they were 14 to 15-years-old.



“The sexual abuse was notably worse to the first pupil who she engaged in acts of sexual intercourse. With the second pupil the abuse was limited to inappropriate kissing.

“The prosecution do not suggest Ms Bowen forced herself on either boy. Viewed superficially, these boys may have appeared willing to engage in flirtatious and sexual activity.

“But the prosecution remind you she was a teacher in a position of trust and authority. By flirting with them and engaging in sexual activity with them she exploited her position for her own sexual gratification.

“As these boys were exploited in that way, any apparent agreement on their part was not genuine consent to the sexual activity. She denied any form of sexual activity, whether that’s kissing or sexual intercourse with either.”



Harrow Crown Court was told Bowen, now aged 64, joined the school in her first job as a chemistry teacher in the 1980s.

She began speaking with the first boy even though he was not in her class and “made him feel special”, it was said.

Jurors heard the pair would spend lunchtime together chatting and sometimes got the school bus home together.

Ms Wolfe added: “As far as he was concerned, their relationship went to the point he thought she was his girlfriend – that he loved her and she loved him.”

Bowen would allegedly encourage the male pupils to “speak and joke openly about sex”.



The boy recalled on one occasion, he and some were flicking through a porn mag and Bowen took it off them.

Jurors heard he expected her to confiscate but she instead “pointed to an image of a naked woman” and said her “p***y” was similar to her own.

This led to the boy taking the bus home with her to Golders Green where they kissed in her flat, the court was told.

Ms Wolfe continued: “For the summer holidays of 1988 he was a regular visitor to that bedroom. He thought they had sex in excess of 20 to 30 times.

“He told police he was never allowed to stay the night. He thought the latest he was allowed to stay was about one o’clock in the morning.”



The court heard the boy’s mum later became suspicious and called Bowen, who denied anything was happening.

In the summer of 1988, the boy was sent to stay with his sister in the north of England and she received “a number of calls” from a woman on the landline, it was said.

When the alleged relationship continued after the holidays, his mum called the school and was told Bowen was no longer working there with “no reason or explanation given”.

Bowen later told the boy she was leaving the UK to stay at a kibbutz in Israel, the court heard.

The boy first disclosed the alleged abuse – including details about the cafe lunches and sex – to a partner, who told him to go to police.



When Bowen was interviewed in 2015, she claimed he was a “bit of a nuisance” and “besotted” with her.

Jurors heard she described the sexual relationship claims as “just pure fantasy”.

As a result of the allegations, Bowen faced a Teaching Regulation Authority hearing in 2022.

The court heard the second pupil read about the TRA hearing online and came forward after encouragement from his wife and family.

He claimed he was “goaded” by other boys at the school into kissing “young and attractive” Bowen.



The pupil also remembered touching her breasts and putting his hand near her crotch – to which “she would not react negatively”, Ms Wolfe said.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Bowen denies eight counts of indecent assault.

The trial continues.

News.title: Remains of foetus found next to river – as cops launch probe into horror discovery
News.content:
TRAGIC FIND Remains of foetus found next to river – as cops launch probe into horror discovery

THE remains of a foetus have been found next to a river as police launch an investigation into the disturbing discovery.

Officers rushed to the River Hodder, Lancashire at 3.13pm yesterday after the remains of a foetus were found beneath Hodder Bridge and Cromwell Bridge in Whalley Road.

The tragic discovery has caused concern, but police have assured locals that a probe is underway.



Cops have urged anyone who has witnessed “anything unusual” to contact them immediately.



A Lancashire Police spokesperson said: “At 3.13pm on Tuesday (August 11), we were called to reports of the discovery of remains of a foetus close to the area beneath Hodder Bridge, Whalley Road, Stonyhurst.

“Officers attended and a scene is currently in place with enquiries ongoing.

“We know this is concerning to hear about, and we want to reassure you that a full investigation is underway to determine how the remains came to be at the location they were found.



“If you were in this area between Sunday, August 9, and Tuesday 11 at 3pm, and witnessed anything unusual, have any dashcam footage from travelling over that bridge, or feel you can help us in any way, please call 101 quoting log 864 of August 11.”

News.title: Do dogs need eclipse glasses? How to keep your pet safe and calm during the solar eclipse today
News.content:
TODAY’S solar eclipse will be the fullest that the UK has seen since 1999, and there won’t be another one this good until 2081.

But while many of us will be squinting skywards through certified glasses or projecting the spectacle, our four-legged friends will almost certainly ignore the whole thing.



Do dogs need eclipse glasses?

No, dogs don’t need eclipse glasses – save your money and spare your dog the indignity.

Dr Jerry Klein, chief veterinary officer at the American Kennel Club, says dogs simply do not look up at the Sun the way people do.



“They know enough not to,” he said, joking that it’s one of the things that makes them smarter than humans.

Angela Gonzalez, associate professor at the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine at the University of Santiago de Compostela and a vet at the Rof Codina University Veterinary Hospital in Lugo, said instinct does the work.



She said: “There would be risks if they were to stare at it, but they wouldn’t normally do that.

“Normally, a dog would just be sniffing around and wouldn’t be staring up at the sky.”

She also urged owners not to buy protective eyewear as most animals aren’t used to wearing anything on their faces, and said no pet should ever be encouraged to look at the eclipse.

The American Animal Hospital Association agrees, adding that putting glasses on a pet causes more stress than the eclipse itself, and that it has found no documented reports of eclipse-related eye damage in pets.



Will the eclipse frighten my dog?

Britain sits outside the path of totality, so the sky will dim rather than darken fully.

The Royal Observatory Greenwich says it will feel more like a cloudy day, or close to dusk, than night.

Observations from the 2017 American eclipse recorded birds falling quiet and returning to nests, crickets and cicadas starting their evening chorus, cats seeking shelter and livestock heading back to barns.

Dogs mostly looked to their owners or lay down.



Prof Gonzalez said a sudden change in light can startle sensitive animals, but normally nothing happens.

The real variable is you – vets warn the genuine risk is owners taking pets into crowded viewing spots, or trying to involve them in the event.

The People’s Dispensary for Sick Animals’ says staying calm yourself and keeping your tone, mood and behaviour as normal as possible reassures your pet.

Whereas getting anxious or acting differently strengthens the idea that there is something to be afraid of.

This advice isn’t new – it is backed up by study done on the effects of a total eclipse on the behaviour of animals in 1932, which was published in the American Academy of Arts & Sciences.



It stated: “Doubtless in some instances, the intelligent animals sensed something unusual in the behaviour of their masters, while probably others … reacted as if a thunderstorm were imminent and became frightened, whimpered or tried to hide away.”

How to keep your pet calm during the eclipse

Treat it as an ordinary evening and don’t encourage them to look up.

Nervous animals are happiest indoors with the curtains drawn.

However, amber heat health alerts are in force across large parts of England today, so the weather is a far bigger threat to your dog this evening than the solar eclipse is.

Keep water available, avoid hot pavements, and think twice about timing a long walk for maximum eclipse.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The general rule of thumb from UK vets is that anything above 25C is too hot to walk a dog — temperatures in London are forecast to still be around 28C at 8pm.

Depending on where you are, the Moon will start to pass the Sun at around 6.15pm, with maximum eclipse between 7.05pm and 7.15pm, and the event finishing just after 8pm.

News.title: Dad left with brain damage & ‘Homer Simpson eyes’ after 5kg steel plate flew off lorry… but driver only got £100 fine
News.content:
HORROR SMASH Dad left with brain damage & ‘Homer Simpson eyes’ after 5kg steel plate flew off lorry… but driver only got £100 fine

A DAD was left with brain damage and “looking like Homer Simpson” after a 5kg steel plate flew off a lorry and smashed through his windscreen.

Anthony Moore, 51, was left fuming after the driver who left him with life changing injuries only received three penalty points and a £100 fine.



The dad-of-three from Heath Hayes, Staffs, said: “My life has been destroyed because somebody failed to do one basic thing – secure a load properly.”

The 51-year-old’s facial injuries and swelling were so bad that his wife later said it left him looking like “Homer Simpson”.



The driver was prosecuted by police for driving with an unsecured load – but Anthony said the punishment is “an insult to every road user”.

Now, after suing the driver’s employer and parent company, Anthony has secured a substantial six-figure out-of-court settlement.



Anthony said: “I wasn’t speeding. I wasn’t taking risks. I was simply driving home from work to my family.

“Within a split second everything I had worked for disappeared. I have lost my career, my independence, my health, and the life I had built with my wife and children.”

He added that his wife has had to give up her job to care for him full time, and the family have spent the last three years trying to rebuild their life.

Anthony said: “I don’t want sympathy. I want accountability. I want companies to understand that securing a load properly isn’t paperwork or box-ticking.

“It is the difference between somebody getting home safely or spending the rest of their life disabled.”



Anthony was minutes from home when the 5kg solid steel plate crashed through the windscreen of his Ford Ranger in September 2023.

It struck his head and his 4×4 careered underneath the same truck and was dragged for almost half a mile before the driver stopped.

The driver was slapped with an £100 fine, three penalty points and a a four week licence suspension from the regional Traffic Commissioner.



Before the crash, Anthony was a senior manager for an events specialist and a devoted dad to his three children, nine, 15 and 21.

His wife Rachel, 45, said: “When I saw Tony I barely recognised him. His face was massively swollen, his eyes were bulging, everything was black and purple.

“He honestly looked like Homer Simpson because the swelling was so severe. There was blood everywhere. It was absolutely horrific.”

Anthony suffered a traumatic brain injury with brain bleeds, and multiple fractures to his skull and face, including a broken eye socket and cheekbone, a fractured right hand, and significant mouth injuries.

After initially surviving his injuries, he developed severe paranoid delusions caused by his brain injury, believing hospital staff were trying to kill him.



He spent just two weeks in hospital, being moved between different wards before eventually being discharged home.

With specialist NHS brain injury rehabilitation limited, the family turned to catastrophic injury lawyers at Express Solicitors for expert help.

They secured funding for intensive neurorehabilitation, psychology, physiotherapy, occupational therapy and specialist support workers while pursuing a legal claim against the driver’s company.

While the case was referred by police to the HSE, they were unable to take any action against the company due to the incident happening on the motorway and the Traffic Commissioner took no further action.

The family later obtained a six-figure settlement against Joseph Ash Galvanizing, a subsidiary company of parent company Hill & Smith PLC.



This will fund Anthony’s future rehabilitation, specialist medical treatment and long-term care.

Catastrophic injury solicitor Nina Ramsden, of Express Solicitors, said: “Tony sustained life-changing injuries in an entirely preventable accident.

“His life changed forever during an ordinary journey home from work.

“His injuries are very complex, but this settlement will ensure Tony can continue receiving the specialist rehabilitation and support he requires while providing financial security for his family’s future.”

A spokesperson for Staffordshire Police said: “A summons was sent to the driver for the insecure load, with a traffic commissioner referral made in relation to the company.



“The driver received points on his licence as well as a fine.

“The Health and Safety Executive was also informed, though no further action was taken by them, due to the incident taking place on a road and not a business premises.”

The West Midlands Traffic Commissioner wrote to the company involved, but took no enforcement action in relation to load security, as policies in place were correct.

The driver attended a conduct hearing and had his vocational licence suspended for 4-weeks.

Hill and Smith PLC – parent company of Joseph Ash Galvanizing – said: “Hill & Smith confirms that Mr Moore sustained a serious injury as a result of a regrettable incident in 2023, with a lorry belonging to its Joseph Ash Galvanizing subsidiary.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The matter has been subject to the appropriate legal and regulatory processes, and we can confirm a settlement was reached, acknowledging the serious nature of the injury.

“We take health and safety across our group extremely seriously and continue to review and strengthen our procedures to help prevent incidents of this nature.”

News.title: Jailed female prison officer, 25, promised to wait until drug kingpin lover served sentence in gushing Valentine’s card
News.content:
'LOVE YOU ALWAYS' Jailed female prison officer, 25, promised to wait until drug kingpin lover served sentence in gushing Valentine’s card

A PRISON officer promised to wait out her drug kingpin lover’s 12-year sentence in a gushing Valentine’s Day card found in the lag’s cell.

Jai Gascoyne, who has since been jailed following her affair, wrote to Dil Nawaz: “Anyone can say I love you but not everyone can wait and prove it”.



The card continued: “Happy Valentine’s Day D, here’s to the first of forever and I can’t wait for the future.”

The 25-year-old prison guard at HMP Buckley Hall signed off “love you always”.



Her heartfelt card was found when Nawaz’s cell was searched after prison anti-corruption officials received intelligence.

Officers also found the 30-year-old wearing a silver bracelet engraved with a “J”, a match to a “D” necklace Gascoyne was wearing when she was searched.

The former prison guard claimed this was for her dad, but she was also found with a second necklace engraved with Arabic script that she could not explain the meaning of.



Manchester Crown Court heard how it was thought to be an Islamic prayer for protection.

Officers later discovered the prison guard had ordered two bracelets and two necklaces with pendants on Amazon.

In Gascoyne’s car officer’s found a ring in a box alongside a love letter also signed off “I love you always”.

The same investigation also uncovered that Nawaz’s brother Haq Nawaz, 32, was involved in an affair with another prison officer, Elle Walron, 27.

The brothers were both locked up for heading a OCG gang with their other brother Asim Nawaz.



It is believed the gang distributed between £2.15m and £3.1m worth of crack cocaine and heroin over a 12-month period.

On top of Haq and Dil Nawaz’s sentences – 13 years and 10 months and 12 years respectively – the pair will now serve an additional 12 months for their secret relationships.

The prison officers were also sentenced on August 7, Gascoyne was handed a 16- month sentence while Walton will serve 13 months



Gascoyne, of Dukinfield, Greater Manchester, pleaded guilty to two counts of misconduct in public office.

She also had inappropriate contact with a further two prisoners, Manchester Crown Court heard.

Walton, of Bacup, Lancashire, pleaded guilty to one count.

Alongside the cards and jewellery, the couples sent hundreds of messages and exchanged gifts and money.

Gascoyne and Dil Nawaz even declared their “love” for each other in their messages and he discussed “wanting to have sex”.



The court heard how he suggested the prison officer could take him to the chapel or “open his door and go in his room.”

Dil Nawaz said he wanted “companionship” as he struggled with his mental health following a prison attack, the court heard.

Meanwhile, his brother had “‘wanted someone to talk to” due to feeling isolated from his family.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Recorder Ben Lawrence said their case “strikes at the heart of the public faith in the prison system”.

He added that the sentences would be a “deterrent” for “the next young female prison officer who considers starting a relationship with a prisoner.”

News.title: Three ways to watch the solar eclipse safely without glasses
News.content:
With most online orders not able to arrive in time and shops running out of stock, it may be too late to buy eclipse glasses for Wednesday evening.

But you can still safely watch the spectacle using some household items.

People in the UK will see a partial eclipse - rather than the total eclipse that will be seen in parts of Spain, Greenland and Iceland - but it is the country's most significant eclipse since 1999.

Experts say enthusiasts should not look directly at the Sun without specialist glasses.

And you shouldn't be tempted to try using sunglasses or dark goggles instead.

They often don't give enough UV protection when looking directly at the Sun and you could end up seriously damaging your eyesight, according to The Royal Astronomical Society.

Here are some viewing methods to try instead.

News.title: Double killer and rapist given whole life sentence
News.content:
A serial sex attacker who had a "morbid fascination" with sex has been jailed for the rest of his life after he was found guilty of murdering two women and raping a third.

Simon Levy, 40, killed Carmenza Valencia-Trujillo, 53, in March 2025 and 39-year-old Sheryl Wilkins five months later. Earlier that year, he raped a third woman in the same Tottenham car park where Wilkins was later found dead.

At the Old Bailey on Wednesday, Judge Mark Lucraft KC sentenced Levy to a whole life order, meaning he will never be released.

The sentence comes after police and the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) apologised over a series of disastrous decisions that left him free to roam the streets.

When Levy carried out the attacks, he was on bail and being monitored by the Met.

The police watchdog is currently examining how he was managed over a four-year period, from his first conviction in September 2021 for sexual assault up to his final arrest in September 2025.

Following Wednesday's sentencing, Met Police Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley said the handling of Levy's case was a "whole system failing".

News.title: Burnham considers disposable BBQ ban over wildfire risks
News.content:
Andy Burnham has said the government is considering a ban on disposable barbecues amid increased wildfire risk driven by this summer's droughts.

The prime minister told reporters single-use grills had been behind a number of recent blazes and people should not be using them "at this moment in time".

Some retailers have already decided to voluntarily stop selling the devices, which have previously attracted warnings from fire chiefs.

It comes as Burnham chairs an emergency Cobra meeting on the government's response to record temperatures in recent months.

Nearly three-quarters of England and all of Wales have been officially declared in drought, creating conditions rife for fire to spread.

The Met Office has issued a rare amber extreme heat warning for Thursday, with temperatures peaking in the mid-to-high 30s across the Midlands and south-east of England, and a high of 38C possible.

Speaking during a visit to Stevenage, Burnham said a disposable barbecue ban was something the government was "certainly going to consider".

"I do want to leave the meeting today with a loud and clear message that we do want people to take the greatest possible care when they are out in the countryside, both in terms of cigarettes, but also those temporary barbecues that we know are causing risk of fires," he added.

News.title: Jasper Carrott says family is 'so proud' of Lucy Davis after cancer diagnosis
News.content:
Actor and comedian Jasper Carrott has spoken about his pride and love for daughter Lucy Davis after she announced she has incurable breast cancer.

The actress, best known for playing receptionist Dawn Tinsley in BBC sitcom The Office, has received an outpouring of support since she revealed her diagnosis on Tuesday.

Carrott, who was one of the most familiar faces on British television over several decades, told BBC News: "This is a very difficult time for the whole family and we have been supporting her in every way possible since her diagnosis.

"We are so grateful for all the support we have had over this trying time and we are very hopeful for her future being what she wants it to be."

He added: "We are so proud of our daughter and love her so much. The way she has conducted herself through many traumatic health issues is a lesson to us all.

"We would request privacy for the coming months, but thanks once again for the love and concern shown by so many people."

Carrott, whose real name is Robert Davis, became a household name in the 1970s thanks to his stand-up comedy and novelty songs.

He has presented programmes such as Canned Carrott, Golden Balls and Carrott's Commercial Breakdown, and acted in comedy series such as The Detectives.

News.title: Messi unsure he will play 'much longer' after father's death
News.content:
Lionel Messi said he is unsure how much longer he will continue playing football as he posted an emotional tribute after his father's death.

Messi's father Jorge was 68 when he died last week following a long illness.

Jorge had been the Argentina forward's agent since he was 14 and watched him become one of the sport's greatest ever players.

"I don't know what I'm going to do without you," eight-time Ballon d'Or winner Messi wrote on social media.

"I don't know how to carry on. I used to just play football, and now I'm really not sure if I'll carry on doing it for much longer.

"You were by my side from the very beginning. We were so close to the end. Why didn't you hang in there just a little longer so we could finish this together?"

Messi captained Argentina as they won the World Cup in 2022 and led them to the 2026 World Cup final, which his side lost 1-0 to Spain, before returning to club side Inter Miami.

He returned home with his family after Jorge passed away in a hospital in his hometown of Rosario, Argentina.

A private funeral took place on Sunday at a cemetery in the town of Perez, on the outskirts of Rosario.

"Dad, I still can't believe you're gone," Messi continued. "It hasn't sunk in, or rather, I don't want it to.

"It's so hard for me to imagine that I'll never see you again, that we'll never talk again. I know you were suffering and that this is for the best, but you left too soon. We still had so much left to enjoy together."

During the World Cup, Messi was brought to tears after scoring the opening goal in Argentina's 3-0 win against Algeria because of a matter he said was "completely unrelated to football". A statement from his family later said Jorge was dealing with a "health-related situation".

Messi added: "You kept asking me to play in one last World Cup, and just days before it started, that's when you took a turn for the worse.

"It was the first time you weren't going to be at a tournament, but Mom kept telling me you'd get better and that you'd be well enough to travel. I kept telling you that we were going to make it to the final so you could come along.

"Every time a game ended, I'd wait for and miss your message. That's when I realised how bad the situation was.

"Even so, I couldn't stop thinking about going as far as possible, to give you time to watch a game. We made it to the final, and you couldn't be there.

"I wanted to win it so I could bring the trophy to you and show you a new one. I couldn't, my legs had nothing left. This time I tried to push past my physical limits, but I couldn't. I never managed to feel right."

Messi made his sixth appearance at a World Cup as he captained Argentina at the 2026 tournament.

He played eight games during the competition, scoring eight goals and registering four assists.

Messi's family relocated to Spain in February 2001 after he was signed by Barcelona aged just 13 and, while his mother and three siblings soon moved back to Rosario, his father stayed with him.

The forward went on to score a record 672 goals in 778 games for Barca, helping the club to win the Champions League four times and La Liga title on 10 occasions.

He joined Paris St-Germain in August 2021 before moving to Inter Miami in July 2023, with his contract at the Major League Soccer side running until 2028.

"Of course, you never missed a single game," said Messi. "How you suffered watching me play and how much you enjoyed it, even though you never gave me much praise.

"You were my dad, my friend and my mentor. You were always exactly the person you needed to be in every moment, and you were never wrong about anything.

"Despite a few disagreements or arguments, you were always right. In the end, things always turned out just as you said they would.

"I'm going to miss you so much, but you'll always be with me, especially in raising my children, because I teach and raise them just as you both did with me.

"Rest in peace, and watch over us from above just as you did here. Thank you for everything.

"I love you, Dad."

Following Messi's emotional tribute, Portugal international Cristiano Ronaldo posted a message to his fellow forward.

"A huge hug to you and yours in these hard times, Leo. Much strength," said the 41-year-old.

Inter Miami co-owner and ex-England international Beckham said: "We are with you and your family, Leo, always."

News.title: Burnham warned Iran war could hit UK growth next year
News.content:
Andy Burnham has been warned that the UK economy could barely grow next year if disruption in the Strait of Hormuz continues until the end of 2026.

Treasury sources have confirmed that internal modelling presented to the new prime minister and chancellor suggests UK GDP growth could be as low as 0.3% in 2027, as first reported by Bloomberg.

Government officials say they routinely plan for all possible scenarios.

The UK economy saw a strong start to the year, but growth then faltered with the conflict in the Middle East affecting some businesses. The Iran war has pushed up oil and fuel prices, and also disrupted supply chains.

On Thursday, official figures will show how much the economy grew between April and June of this year.

Economists are expecting growth of 0.4% for the three months.

Burnham and Chancellor John Healey were presented with a reasonable worst-case scenario of the Strait of Hormuz remaining effectively closed for the next five months, and no permanent US-Iran peace deal until the new year.

The Treasury modelling for that scenario was that the UK economy would grow by 0.9% over 2026 - slightly under the 1.1% forecast by the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) in March.

The prospect was much dimmer for next year, with just 0.3% growth projected - much lower than the OBR's 1.6% forecast for 2027.

Under the modelling, inflation would peak at 4.3% in the first three months of next year. It currently stands at 2.6%, just above the Bank of England's 2% target.

The prime minister and chancellor will face pressure to use the upcoming Budget on 28 October to ease the financial burden on households and businesses.

Since taking office three weeks ago, Burnham has announced policies including the removal of VAT from domestic electricity bills and bringing forward an already planned end to "subscription traps".

But this week he told the BBC's Wake up to Money the announcements, aimed at tackling the cost of living, are not enough on their own, hinting at further support.

He has asked Healey to look at what more the government can do on the cost of living in the Budget, with the chancellor saying it will be his "main focus".

But Healey has said he will oversee "strong fiscal discipline" â which will limit how much the government has to spend.

Burnham has said his government will stick to the party's 2024 manifesto pledges not to increase people's income tax, VAT or National Insurance contributions.

He also promised to follow the fiscal rules imposed by former Chancellor Rachel Reeves, which include a pledge to balance day-to-day spending with tax revenues by the end of the decade.

News.title: X-Men star Nicholas Hoult joins cast of Harry Potter TV show
News.content:
Nicholas Hoult, known for his roles in X-Men, Superman and Mad Max: Fury Road, has been cast in the hotly anticipated Harry Potter TV series.

The English actor, 36, will play Hogwarts professor Gilderoy Lockhart - who was portrayed by Sir Kenneth Branagh in the films.

The TV adaptation of JK Rowling's best-selling books will reach screens this Christmas, although Hoult will not be seen until season two.

In the stories, Lockhart was a celebrity author of books such as Magical Me before joining Hogwarts as a Defence Against the Dark Arts teacher in Harry's second year.

HBO announced the casting, external by quoting the title of Lockhart's autobiography and one of his famous lines: "Magical me indeed. Now, how many autographs would you like? Nicholas Hoult has been cast as Gilderoy Lockhart in season two of the new HBO original Harry Potter series."

News.title: How the weather will affect your viewing
News.content:
One of the most spectacular solar eclipses the UK has seen for decades is taking place on Wednesday 12 August.

From around 18:00 BST, the Moon will begin moving across the face of the Sun, creating a partial solar eclipse across the UK.

At its peak, around 90% of the Sun will be covered from London. In Cornwall, as much as 95% of the Sun could be obscured.

Depending on where you are in the UK, it will peak between 19:02 and 19:16 BST.

News.title: Early release scheme risks more serious crimes, probation chief inspector warns
News.content:
The chief inspector of probation for England and Wales has told the BBC the early release of thousands of prisoners could lead to "a serious sexual or violent offence or even murder" because of the demands on probation staff to monitor offenders.

The government is set to release 5,000 offenders from October as part of new laws to create more space in overcrowded prisons.

Probation officers supervise offenders after prison sentences and check they follow the terms of their release, such as sticking to curfews and not taking drugs.

A Ministry of Justice spokesperson said "protecting the public is our top priority", adding it had invested in probation and hiring trainee officers.

But Martin Jones, His Majesty's Chief Inspector of probation for England and Wales, told the BBC that "ultimately I'm not fully confident that the probation system will be able to cope with this massive work and there's a risk that things will go wrong".

"Probation services are already under unprecedented pressure.

"I mean, they're managing a caseload of 258,000 cases, that's nearly three times the number that are in our prisons, and obviously the early release scheme will be increasing that pressure considerably."

On Tuesday, 50 police chiefs across the UK signed a letter to the prime minister urging him to pursue "every legal option" to prevent the early release of PC Andrew Harper's killers under the scheme.

They called for called for greater consideration of victims when prisoners have their sentences altered, adding: "Families across the country are now facing the distress of learning that offenders may be released earlier than they understood when sentence was passed."

They also welcomed Burnham's intervention on Tuesday, when he said he was "confident" the early release of Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, who were jailed for 13 years for manslaughter in 2020, in January could be stopped.

Shadow home secretary Chris Philp told BBC Breakfast the early release plans had "put public safety at risk as well as disrespecting victims and undermining confidence in the criminal justice system".

He urged Burnham to "pay attention and listen" to the senior police officers, adding he had "never seen every chief constable in the country write to the prime minister directly in this way".

Philip and Nick Timothy, the Conservative shadow justice secretary, wrote to Burnham on Tuesday urging him to introduce emergency primary legislation in September to amend the Sentencing Act 2026.

The letter said grooming gang perpetrators, including those convicted of indecent assault, and those convicted of the manslaughter of an emergency worker should be exempt from the early release scheme.

News.title: I share concerns over Arday appointment, says Cambridge University head
News.content:
The vice-chancellor of the University of Cambridge has said she understands the concerns raised by the appointment of Jason Arday and shares them too.

In a letter to staff, Prof Deborah Prentice acknowledged the "anger and anxiety around this damaging and difficult case".

The university head also announced Cambridge's investigation would be independent and carried out by senior academics from within and beyond Cambridge and will begin "as soon as possible".

Arday resigned as a Cambridge professor of sociology of education last week amid allegations of plagiarism and questions about some of his achievements.

The 41-year-old - who became Cambridge's youngest ever black professor in 2023 - denies any plagiarism and said the recent furore had led to "an unrelenting level of public scrutiny and personal attack".

In a letter to university staff, Prof Deborah Prentice said: "I fully understand the concerns being raised across the University and well beyond it, regarding Jason Arday's appointment and I share them...

"We will now investigate the circumstances around his appointment by the faculty of education back in 2022 and his time here in Cambridge since his appointment nearly four years ago.

"That investigation, as you say, should be thorough and transparent, and will be carried out independently by senior academics from within and beyond Cambridge."

The findings of the investigation, previously announced on Friday, will inform a review into the process for the appointment of senior academic roles, the university has said.

Prentice added "our staff of colour are highly valued, for their scholarship, their achievements, and the contributions they make" and said the case "should not be used to cast aspersions on their work or the legitimacy of their roles at Cambridge".

Cambridge had previously said allegations of plagiarism regarding Arday's thesis and some journal publications had been investigated by Liverpool John Moores University (LMJU) and the journals in question.

LJMU - which awarded his PhD in 2015 - had investigated the allegations that were made last year, and found he did not commit plagiarism.

In an interview with the Times, Arday defended himself by arguing that he had not received adequate supervision during his PhD given his autism and "learning disabilities".

The University of Cambridge said it had advised people to contact the relevant institution or pass on complaints.

But after Cambridge announced its own investigation, some academics pushed for the inquiry to be independent, questioning whether the university could adequately investigate its own processes.

It is not yet clear how the independent investigation will work or who will lead it. The university said it will look at the circumstances around his appointment by the faculty of education in 2022 and his time in Cambridge since his appointment.

Arday worked as a PE teacher before earning his doctorate at LMJU and going on to become an associate professor at Durham University and professor of sociology of education at the University of Glasgow.

Glasgow has also announced a review into Arday's previous academic post.

When he resigned from his post, Arday said he was not a "liar" and that his resignation "should not be mistaken for an acceptance of the narratives that have surrounded me."

News.title: Estonia rejects proposals to take prisoners from UK jails
News.content:
The Estonian government has rejected the idea of taking prisoners from the UK to help ease the overcrowding crisis in British jails.

Justice Minister Liisa Pakosta told the BBC Estonia would not rent jail cells to other countries while it was housing criminals from Sweden in its half-empty Tartu prison under a deal signed last week.

The Conservatives and Reform UK have both suggested renting cells in foreign prisons, including in Estonia, to free up space and prevent the early releases of some offenders in England and Wales.

The Labour government also explored the idea in 2024 but talks with Estonia came to nothing.

Pakosta said Estonia had received no proposals to rent its prison space from the UK, adding that if one was to be made "our answer would be unequivocal - in Margaret Thatcher's famous words: No. No. No."

She added: "Such a proposal would not merely be mistaken, misguided or unacceptable; it would deserve to be rejected outright."

Thatcher memorably repeated "no" three times in 1990 speech, as she fiercely rejected calls for deeper political and economic integration of the European Community, which later evolved into the European Union.

In 2024, the Labour government, when Sir Keir Starmer was prime minister, held talks with Estonia to discuss the Baltic state's policy to house some prisoners from abroad.

Pakosta previously told the BBC she had met then-UK Justice Secretary Shabana Mahmood in Lithuania.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham's government is planning to release thousands of prisoners early this October, as it scrambles to free up space in jails almost at 100% capacity.

On Monday, Downing Street did not rule out renting space in foreign prisons, when asked by reporters if the government was considering doing so.

A No 10 spokesperson said the government was focused on "creating that extra capacity within the system domestically".

"In terms of renting prison places abroad, it's just not a quick fix," the spokesperson added.

"It will require primary legislation underpinned by a complex international agreement which would take several years to agree."

A government source told the BBC that renting foreign prison space would not help with the short-term crisis in jails.

Burnham has ordered the justice secretary to come up with a plan to create more space in jails by September.

He said the plan would be based on removing more foreign national offenders from prisons, releasing some offenders on indefinite sentences, and using space in women's jails for male inmates.

News.title: Semi-pro footballer filmed driving at 191mph
News.content:
A semi-professional footballer who was filmed driving at 191mph has been jailed.

Connor Charlton, 32, was also involved in a scam where other drivers took penalty points for speeding offences in return for cash, the Crown Prosecution Service said.

The centre forward, who plays for Nostell Miners Welfare FC in the Northern Counties East League, was seen in footage drifting his BMW at a roundabout, almost crashing into a van. A passenger also filmed him driving at 191mph on a motorway.

Charlton, from Hunslet, was sentenced on Wednesday at Leeds Crown Court to four years in jail and banned from driving for four years and seven months.

He had admitted 10 counts of dangerous driving and four offences of perverting the course of justice.

News.title: Windermere signs to warn of algae poisoning risk
News.content:
Dozens of signs warning people about the dangers of algae poisoning are to be placed around England's largest lake.

About 40 notice boards alerting visitors to blue-green algae blooms, which can produce toxins that make humans ill and be fatal to pets, will be installed at Windermere, in the Lake District.

Blooms occur naturally but are more frequent during warm, dry weather and are exacerbated by nutrients from phosphate in pollutants such as sewage.

Funded by the Environment Agency (EA), a further 40 signs will be placed at other locations across Cumbria.

The Love Windermere Partnership, which includes organisations such as the EA, Lake District National Park Authority and United Utilities, said it was installing the permanent signs in response to requests for "clearer and more consistent public information".

As well as explaining what blue-green algae looks like, the notices will provide guidance on where to find current information about blooms and how to report suspected sightings using the Bloomin' Algae app, external.

The microscopic organisms can look like blue-green paint, scum or greenish-brown discolouration.

News.title: Serious failings found in new military crimes unit, leaked report finds
News.content:
A leaked Ministry of Defence (MoD) report, obtained by the BBC, has highlighted serious failings in a new military command set up to investigate the most severe crimes, including rape and sexual assault.

The Defence Serious Crime Command (DSCC) was launched after the death of 19-year-old Gunner Jaysley Beck. An inquest found the Army's mishandling of sexual assault and harassment complaints made by Beck contributed to her taking her own life, and exposed "systemic failings".

However, an internal review highlighted ongoing concerns with the unit and warned the military still risks failing victims.

The MoD said the findings had been accepted and significant work has been undertaken since.

The DSCC was created in 2022 to investigate serious crimes independently, outside the military's chain of command.

However, the BBC can reveal that an internal review, which was carried out between 21 August 2025 and 12 November 2025 and overseen by a former senior civilian police officer, concluded that if the DSCC was subjected to scrutiny similar to civilian police forces there would be "a significant risk of (it) being graded as inadequate".

In a statement, the MoD said the review was commissioned "to provide honest challenge, identify areas of improvement and to help ensure the highest standards for victims and witnesses".

It added that following the findings, the DSCC had carried out significant work "including further investment in victim and witness support, strengthening governance and safeguarding arrangements and accrediting investigators to nationally recognised policing standards".

The DSCC was committed to transparency, continuous improvement and ensuring victims receive the support and service they deserve, the statement continued.

News.title: Man, 102, in critical condition after alleged pub assault
News.content:
A 102-year-old man is in a critical condition after allegedly being assaulted at a pub.

Emergency services were called to The Crow's Nest pub in Cwmbran, Torfaen, at about 22:25 BST on 1 August, and the man was taken to hospital.

A 56-year-old man from Llanelli, Carmarthenshire, was arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm, and has since been released under investigation.

Gwent Police is appealing for witnesses and want to speak to anyone who was in the pub between 22:00 and 23:00 on the night of the incident.

News.title: Family almost miss £1m lotto win after ignoring calls
News.content:
A family almost missed out on a Â£1m lottery jackpot after unknowingly ignoring calls and emails notifying them that they had won.

Builder Mark Jefferson from Ilminster, Somerset, ignored the National Lottery's notifications for nine days before reluctantly answering the phone.

Jefferson, his wife and their four children set up the syndicate in July 2025 to celebrate his birthday.

"Knowing the family has opportunities we have never imagined before is the best feeling in the world," Jefferson said.

The family syndicate matched five main numbers and the Bonus Ball in the lottery draw on 24 June.

Jefferson's daughter, Alexandra, chose the winning numbers.

The head of the Metropolitan Police has called on the criminal justice system "to do its job better", warning that dangerous offenders are being granted bail "day in, day out".

Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley criticised the courts for repeatedly releasing serial sex attacker Simon Levy on bail, while also conceding there were “things we could have done better”.

Speaking to broadcasters on Wednesday after the 40-year-old received a whole-life order for murder and rape, Sir Mark said: "He was repeatedly by the police put before the courts seeking remanding in custody. The police were saying this guy is too dangerous to be on the streets, and between CPS and the courts, they kept bailing him."

He argued that it was "not acceptable for a struggling criminal justice system to put increasing amount of risks on the street, and then say to the police ‘we’re going to give you a bigger and bigger list of dangerous people to monitor’ and then focus all the criticism on us if we don’t do it as well as we could".

Sir Mark insisted he was not attempting to "absolve" the Met of its own duties, but maintained that "dangerous people need remanding in custody".

"We’re seeing far too many cases day in and day out – knife carriers, sex offenders, who are being bailed when a few years ago they would’ve been remanded in custody and we can’t carry all of that load in communities. We will do everything we can do to do better, but the justice system needs to carry more of the load than it is at the moment, rather than passing it back onto the streets," he said.

Simon Levy was jailed for life on Wednesday ( British Transport Police )

Pressed on the role played by police in stopping Levy in his tracks, Sir Mark noted the force had "already apologised", while pointing to "complexities" in the case.

He said: "We need a justice system that helps us rather than keep putting dangerous people back on the streets when that’s obviously the wrong answer…

"But you can’t just put all the risk into communities, not take dangerous people into prison when there’s a strong case to do so, and then say to the police, you just carry all that risk, and we’ll blame you when it goes wrong. The justice system needs to do its job better."

Victims’ Commissioner Claire Waxman described the case as "appalling", stating that it "represents one of the most shocking examples of systemic failure in recent years".

She added: "A dangerous serial sex offender repeatedly came to the attention of multiple agencies, yet critical opportunities to identify the risk he posed, share information and take protective action were missed. The consequences in this case were devastating."

She stated that she was "gravely concerned these failures and oversights will not be one-offs" in light of the criminal justice system being under "unprecedented pressure".

News.title: Voices: ‘Only the courts can keep someone in prison’: Readers reject calls to block PC Harper killers’ early release
News.content:

We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it. Your support makes all the difference. Read more

Downing Street is under mounting pressure over its failure to block the early release of two of PC Andrew Harper’s killers, with a police chief calling the decision “indefensible” and more than 880,000 people signing a petition demanding Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers stay behind bars.

But among Independent readers, the anger cuts in an unexpected direction.

Rather than backing calls for a one-off exemption, many commenters pushed back hard against the idea of government intervening in a single case at all, arguing it would corrode judicial independence and set a dangerous precedent for how sentences get decided.

Others aimed their fury not at Andy Burnham but at the Conservative government they blame for leaving the prison system without enough capacity to avoid the early release scheme in the first place.

Not everyone agreed – some readers argued cop killers should be a clear exception to any early release scheme, while others questioned the fairness of grouping Cole and Bowers, convicted as passengers under joint enterprise law, with PC Harper’s actual killer.

Here’s what you had to say:

Only the courts can keep someone in prison

In the UK neither the government nor the police can keep someone in prison – only the courts can do that.

It is very worrying that a “senior” policeman thinks differently, or that we live in a police state with laws that are bendable by the authorities.

Magma

Blame the Tory government, not Burnham

The only ones spitting in the face of police officers – and in the faces of every victim of crime whose perpetrator is being released early – are the Tory government. What they did to the prison system, and how they left our justice system, is nothing short of corrupt, neglectful and downright dangerous. Burnham can’t refuse to release one set of criminals early without others jumping on the bandwagon and demanding the same. He should explain to the public exactly how the Tories left the prison system, and make clear that if criminals aren’t released early this autumn, the entire justice system – including the power of arrest and our courts – collapses.

Amy

Blocking releases for one case corrupts judicial independence

That criticism is asking the government to do something that would violate proper democratic separation of powers. In most functioning democracies, judges sentence according to law, parole boards assess release conditions, and the executive enforces but doesn’t override judicial decisions. If the government could simply block prisoner releases for political reasons – because a case generated public outrage or a victim’s family campaigned – that’s exactly the corruption of judicial independence that democracies are supposed to prevent. Every sentenced prisoner’s release would then depend on whether their case attracted enough media attention or political pressure.

Nixda

Prisons were already full when Labour took office

This is a problem that arises because of the previous Conservative government’s negligence and neglect of the prison service. Prisons were full when Labour took office.

junia

Hard cases make bad law

It’s a bit of a truism to say that hard cases make bad law, but it also contains a hefty grain of truth. There are already other campaigns started by grieving relatives to get people who committed manslaughter or death by dangerous driving kept behind bars, but the government can’t cave in to all of them because the law and the way it is applied has to be impartial. I don’t like the idea of these people being let out, but I don’t see how it can be avoided. The prison release scheme can’t be cancelled because the UK is about to run out of prison cells, and that will bring the entire criminal justice system to a halt. Going forward, maybe the answer is to reform the definition of manslaughter to include various grades of culpability, but that can’t be applied retrospectively.

Tanaquil2

Special rules for individuals break down law and order

The driver of the vehicle is not eligible for early release. The moment you set out “special rules” for some individuals, over and above the sentence they received for their crime, you start to break down law and order in the UK. Focus your anger on failed Tory neoliberal austerity, which broke the UK, and the justice and prisons system – just one of many examples of expensive failure.

wolfie

The sentencing judge should have accounted for this

Much as I find the release of these people appalling, I cannot see how we can make special cases. The abhorrent nature of their crimes should have been taken fully into account by the sentencing judge, so they must be treated as any other person given the same sentence.

much0ado

They were passengers, not the driver

People should be careful what they wish for when demanding politicians interfere in judicial decisions. The public will have their views on the two who were convicted. But as a point of information, probably worth remembering, they were passengers in a car fleeing a crime. They were convicted of manslaughter not because of direct action but “joint enterprise” responsibility. Clearly it will not make any difference to some, particularly not PC Harper’s grieving family, but it’s indicative of a lack of nuance in the system.

hollybaxter

Legislate by offence class, not by name

The answer to the dilemma raised by some here is that the government can change, by general legislation, the rules governing early release. This could be a general rule applying to a class of offences (e.g. those resulting in the death of an emergency worker), not a government decision aimed at the two individuals specifically.

Musil

Burnham’s first response was the right one

Burnham’s first response was the correct one. We can’t be singling out cases for more severe punishment just because the media brings it to public attention. Where the focus should be is keeping dangerous individuals behind bars. What is the likelihood of these men killing someone else? I would speculate almost none. Their case was very circumstantial and not premeditated, which is why they were only convicted of manslaughter.

Ian Robinson

They’ll be released under existing rules regardless

They will in any case be released soon under the existing rules regarding serving half the judge-determined sentence with good behaviour. The arbitrary removal of this rule would make prison officers’ jobs impossible, and could theoretically lead to a doubling of the number of prison places required.

GrymSdijk

How does a court really measure remorse?

I find this issue of “showing remorse” as a factor in sentencing difficult to understand. I’m sure many criminals will be experts at “showing remorse” if they know it’s a factor in their sentencing. Many others, and especially teenage boys, will simply not have the mental and emotional equipment to handle their remorse, and so will behave inappropriately. And many, of course, will not feel remorse. But how does a court tell the difference?

margsmeanders

Early release is needed – but not for cop killers

Release of prisoners early is needed, unfortunately, due to a distinct lack of forward planning by previous governments. However, cop killers and attackers on police should not be allowed within the early release cohort, not just for this situation but for the rule of law in general. Now it is up to this government to try and fix this mess.

Theframe

Billionaire Mark Walter is reportedly selling the Los Angeles Lakers to former Disney CEO Bob Iger and venture capitalist Josh Kushner for a record-breaking $12.5 billion.

"As lifelong NBA fans, we are deeply honored for the opportunity to become stewards of the Los Angeles Lakers, one of the most iconic sports franchises in the world. We have immense respect for the leadership and vision of Jerry and Jeanie Buss," Kushner and Iger told ESPN in a statement Wednesday. "Our long-term commitment is to build on that foundation, compete at the highest level, and serve this extraordinary team, its fans, and the city of Los Angeles."

The pair had been involved in the NBA’s expansion process in Las Vegas before unexpectedly shifting their focus to the Lakers and making an aggressive offer to buy the team, sources told ESPN.

The shocking sale comes just one year after Walter, the CEO and chairman of diversified holding company TWG Global, acquired a controlling stake in the Lakers from the Buss family for an estimated $10 billion valuation, setting a record at the time.

“Owning the Los Angeles Lakers has been one of the great honors of my life – an extraordinary investment, but what I will carry with me is the community, the fans, and a city that treats this team as family,” Walter, who purchased the franchise just last year, said in a statement to ESPN. “I am grateful to Jeanie Buss, the Buss family, the players, and the staff for welcoming me into this chapter. The Lakers belong to Los Angeles, and I have every confidence the best is still ahead.”

open image in gallery Bob Iger, 75, ended his second stint as Disney CEO in March ( Getty Images for Vanity Fair )

Walter, 66, has investments across several professional sports teams. Through TWG Global, he has interests in the Los Angeles Dodgers, Los Angeles Sparks, Premier League soccer club Chelsea and the Professional Women’s Hockey League. He also owns several auto racing teams through TWG Motorsports, including Cadillac’s Formula 1 team.

The reported deal involves only Walter’s ownership of the Lakers, according to ESPN.

Walter built his fortune in the insurance industry and is also facing a federal investigation involving alleged tax fraud at other companies tied to him.

Kushner, 41, is the founder and CEO of venture capital firm Thrive Capital and the co-founder and vice chairman of Oscar Health. In April, Thrive Eternal, a permanent investment vehicle from Thrive Capital, acquired a minority, non-controlling stake in the San Francisco Giants.

He is also the younger brother of Jared Kushner, a former adviser to President Donald Trump who is married to Ivanka Trump. Josh Kushner is married to supermodel Karlie Kloss.

open image in gallery Josh Kushner, 41, is the founder and CEO of venture capital firm Thrive Capital and the co-founder and vice chairman of Oscar Health ( Getty Images )

Iger, 75, meanwhile, recently ended his second stint as Disney CEO, handing the role to Josh D’Amaro in March. Iger also has experience in professional sports ownership, as he and his wife, Willow Bay, became controlling owners of the National Women's Soccer League club Angel City FC in July 2024.

Iger and Kushner would take over the Lakers as the franchise enters the post-LeBron James era.

James left in July for the Philadelphia 76ers after eight seasons in LA and one NBA title, leaving Luka Doncic as the team’s new centerpiece. The Lakers have also added big man Walker Kessler and re-signed guard Austin Reaves.

News.title: Harry Jowsey accuses Netflix of editing sexual sound effects into Let’s Marry Harry: ‘Certainly was not us’
News.content:

Harry Jowsey has claimed that Netflix added sexual sound effects to exaggerate a scene in Let’s Marry Harry.

The 29-year-old reality star, known for appearing on the Netflix dating shows Too Hot to Handle and Perfect Match, is the love interest in streamer’s latest offering, a Bachelor-style format where Jowsey dates 20 women who want to marry him.

In an Instagram video shared Monday, Jowsey claimed that a kissing scene between him and one of the finalists, Dannelle Davidson, was exaggerated by the producers and editors to make it seem like they were having sex.

In episode two of the eight-part series, the pair are filmed kissing on a bed, before moving to a hallway where there are no hidden cameras.

The pair are still wearing their mics when subtitles show Jowsey saying, “Happy birthday, darling, I adore you,” and moaning and grunting sounds begins before the episode ends on a cliffhanger.

open image in gallery Dannelle Davidson and Harry Jowsey have both said they only kissed in ‘Let’s Marry Harry,’ despite sound effects suggesting otherwise ( Netflix )

While that scene suggested that they were having sex, Jowsey claimed via an Instagram Q&A on Monday that the sounds had been added to exaggerate the drama.

“We were just making out,” he said of the scene. “I don’t know where they pulled that audio from, or who that was in that audio, but it was certainly not us.”

The Independent has contacted Netflix for comment.

Jowsey claimed that the producers made it seem “a little more exaggerated” than what actually happened for extra shock factor.

“It’s a TV show and every three days is one episode, so of course they’re going to put the crazy stuff in there,” he explained. “They needed a big cliffhanger on the end of that episode to keep you hooked, to keep you watching. Again, the greatness of TV to make something seem a little more exaggerated than they actually are.”

He reiterated that “we were literally just kissing in the closet in the early episodes.”

Davidson also shared her perspective Monday on TikTok: “The birthday scene is funny to me. Of course, it looked like we were maybe getting a little hot and heavy in the closet. We were making out, and I enjoyed it. It was my birthday. Sue me.”

In the show, Jowsey did hook up with finalist Amber Mozo, but lied to the other women about it after Mozo asked him to keep their intimate moment private.

open image in gallery In ‘Let’s Marry Harry,’ Harry Jowsey dates 20 women before deciding who he wants to marry ( Netflix )

Mozo and Davidson are the final two vying for Jowsey’s hand in marriage on the finale of Let’s Marry Harry, which airs August 12.

Some of the women participating in the show have claimed online that they were never told by casting producers that it would end in a wedding.

Contestant Rickiyah “KiKi” McGrady shared in a TikTok video over the weekend: “Did you know that about half of the girls who were on Let’s Marry Harry did not know that Harry Jowsey would be the man they would be engaged to and possibly marrying when they were cast for a dating show?”

“Did you know that I was one of those girls?”

Two more cast members backed up McGrady’s story in the comments section, with Debralee Tomberlin writing, “Like we did NOT know what we were signing up for,” and Shaine Hinson adding, “They told me literally four days before I was like wtf.”

Let’s Marry Harry was executive produced by Call Her Daddy host Alex Cooper, Matt Kaplan, Mina Lefevre and showrunner David Friedman.

Jowsey’s friends, Amanda Kloots, Georgia Hassarati and Sonny Henty, appear in the show to help him choose his future wife. The trio observe his connections and decide which women would go on dates and be eliminated.

Cooper also appeared on the show, in episode seven, to give advice to Jowsey.

Federal employees can once again indulge in TikTok videos after the White House lifted its ban on the platform.

In 2022, former President Joe Biden prohibited the use of the app on federal devices, citing fears that it was collecting data for the Chinese government. The Office of Budget Management was tasked with developing the guidelines for enforcing the ban.

The White House reversed the ban in a memo dated for Monday but released on Tuesday, according to Politico.

“TikTok is no longer a ‘covered application’ for purposes of the No TikTok on Government Devices Act,” Office of Management and Budget Director Russell Vought wrote in the memo.

In January, TikTok's Chinese owner, ByteDance, sold the majority of its shares to U.S. investors — including Larry Ellison's Oracle — to prevent it from being banned on American devices.

TikTok is no longer banned on federal devices following new guidance from the Department of Justice ( Reuters )

TikTok was temporarily blocked in the U.S. last year ahead of the divestment agreement.

Last month, the Department of Justice adjusted its stance on the app. The DOJ's Office of Legal Counsel determined that the U.S. version of the app — the version created by the ByteDance divestment in January — was not subject to the 2022 ban.

After the July 21 policy change, several federal agencies launched their own accounts on the app. The Treasury Department, the Department of Transportation, and the Department of Health and Human Services all started TikTok accounts following the July decision.

The White House has had an account since last August, well before ByteDance sold off its shares to Oracle and other investors.

Lawmakers tried for years to ban the app in the U.S., which ultimately led to the 2024 law forcing ByteDance to divest or be barred from operating in the U.S.

While the new guidance allows federal employees to once again use the app, there are still bans on it elsewhere in the government.

Both chambers of Congress maintain a TikTok ban on congressional devices, and there are several states that have also banned the app's use on employee phones and computers. Texas and Virginia both ban TikTok on government devices.

While some federal employees may be racing to download the app back onto their work phones, the state of Pennsylvania is preparing to take the app to court. Its concerns are less about security and more about child safety.

Pennsylvania's Attorney General Dave Sunday announced a lawsuit against TikTok alleging that it fails to protect children from age-inappropriate content on its app.

The civil lawsuit claims that the app's recommended age rating — 13+ — is misleading as children can still access adult material on the platform.

He also accuses the app of being addictive and detrimental to children's brains.

"TikTok has built its empire based on a model of addictiveness at all costs, and expanded that empire using deception about what sort of content is viewable for kids," Sunday said, according to ABC6. "This is not an indictment against modern technology, or a scolding assessment of social media as a whole – rather, this is an action to hold accountable a company that values dollars over mental wellness."

TikTok issued a statement pushing back on the lawsuit.

"This lawsuit relies on misleading and inaccurate claims and deliberately ignores the concrete safety measures TikTok has voluntarily implemented to support the well-being of our community. Teen accounts have 50 preset safety, privacy and security settings built-in, and TikTok's Family Pairing tools give parents direct control over screen time and content filters. We will vigorously defend against these claims."

The company did not immediately comment on the Department of Justice's new guidance.

News.title: Teenage boys arrested after police officer injured by car
News.content:

Read our Privacy notice

Six teenage boys have been arrested after a police officer was hit by a car while investigating a suspected burglary in Sunderland.

Northumbria Police said they received a report of a suspected burglary from an address in the Burdon area of the city at 6.45am.

It was reported that a car had been stolen and driven into the Durham force’s area.

The vehicle was spotted parked on Cooperative Terrace in Sunderland just after 8.30am.

Police said when an officer approached on foot and attempted to secure the stolen vehicle, it drove away, hitting another parked car and injured the officer.

The Durham Constabulary officer was taken to hospital with non-life threatening injuries after the incident on Wednesday morning.

Six boys – aged between 13 and 17 – have been arrested in connection with the report and are in police custody.

open image in gallery Total police-recorded crime in England and Wales has fallen by 1% year on year (Amanda Rose/Alamy/PA) ( Alamy/PA )

The road is currently closed to traffic and officers are expected to remain on scene for a number of hours.

Detective Chief Inspector Rebecca Fenney, of Northumbria Police, said: “Firstly, we’d like to extend our thoughts to the officer from our neighbouring police force who has been injured in this incident.

“Police officers attend work with the sole intention to help people – not to be hurt in the line of duty.

“We wish this officer a speedy recovery and we’d like to thank him and his colleagues for their assistance with the response to the initial report.

“Our investigation remains at an early stage, however we already have got six suspects in custody.

“We’re aware this incident will have caused concern and disruption in the local community.

“As this is a live investigation, we ask the public not to speculate on the circumstances or comment on social media.

“Officers will remain in the area, and we would ask anyone with further concerns, or information to report, including CCTV, dashcam, or mobile phone footage, to get in touch with us.”

Assistant Chief Constable Richie Allen, from Durham Constabulary, said: “Our thoughts are with the officer who sustained injuries during the incident.

“Thankfully, he has since been discharged from hospital and we wish him a speedy recovery.”

News.title: UK economy ‘may grow by only 0.3% next year if Middle East disruption goes on’
