In a recent press briefing, Warsh said the Fed cannot use a "magic wand" to undo years of above-target inflation and must stay patient as price growth cools gradually.

One of the Fed's key jobs is to keep inflation near 2%, a level policymakers say keeps prices stable, supports steady economic growth, and helps prevent deeper downturns.

President Donald Trump has also said inflation is still too high for many families, pointing to rent and grocery bills as signs that the cost of living remains a major concern.

Financial markets reacted calmly to the latest figures, with stocks little changed as the figures were broadly in line with market expectations.

Recent labour market concerns have also softened expectations for a rate increase, after July's report showed a loss of jobs.

World.title: Danube river's low water levels reveal remains of WWII soldiers and motorcycle
World.content:
The bodies of two World War Two German soldiers have been found in Budapest's Danube river, due to record-low water levels after an intense drought.

Found alongside their remains were the identification tags of the two soldiers, a largely intact German army Wehrmacht motorcycle, a wedding ring and a Kuban shield - a combat badge of the Wehrmacht, the German War Graves Commission said.

The remarkable finds have sparked hope that some families could finally discover the fates of their ancestors, more than 80 years on from the war.

"Now begins a puzzle, in which we will try to determine the identity of the two dead," Arne Schrader, of the German War Graves Commission, told German newspaper Bild.

The wreck in the Danube was reportedly discovered on 2 August, when a passersby reported part of the motorcycle protruding from the rocks on the riverbank in downtown Budapest.

The team also found anti-tank mines, leading to the temporary closure of the riverbank as a bomb disposal unit was deployed.

Some of the items found in the river, notably the identification tags and motorcycle, are remarkably well-preserved due to the mixture of harbour sludge and oil found on the river bed, the German War Graves Commission said.

The commission is a German non-profit organisation that searches, recovers and buries the war dead on behalf of the German government.

The motorcycle is thought to be a DKW NZ 350-1 model, the organisation said, which was produced specifically for wartime use from 1944.

The commission added that of the two tags found, one belonged to a Wehrmacht soldier, and the other to a member of the Waffen-SS, which was declared a criminal organisation responsible for war crimes at the Nuremberg Trials.

World.title: Singapore and S Korea pull Trader Joe's seasoning over poppy seeds
World.content:
Singapore and South Korea have pulled Trader Joe's Everything But the Bagel seasoning from e-commerce platforms because it contains poppy seeds.

While they do not naturally contain opiates, poppy seeds are banned in both countries because they can get contaminated with opiates by fluid in the poppy plant during harvesting.

More than 20 online listings of the popular seasoning have been removed, Singapore's Central Narcotics Bureau said on Wednesday.

Last week, Seoul authorities said the seasoning tested positive for morphine and codeine, which are opiates found in the plant's sap.

Apart from poppy seeds, the product also contains sesame seeds, sea salt, minced garlic and minced onion. It was released by American grocery chain Trader Joe's in 2017.

Authorities in Singapore have urged anyone who has bottles of the seasoning to dispose of them.

"Singapore adopts a strict policy of zero tolerance towards controlled drugs," the narcotics bureau said, according to a CNA report.

"The possession, consumption, importation, exportation, manufacturing and trafficking of any controlled drug, even in trace amounts, is an offence under the Misuse of Drugs Act," it said.

In South Korea, investigators say some people brought the seasoning back home as souvenirs from their overseas trips before listing it for resale.

Some did so without realising it contained controlled substances, while others did so knowingly, according to a report by The Korea Herald.

"Even if a product is legally sold overseas, it may be classified as a narcotic substance or a prohibited import in Korea, so particular caution is required," a police official said.

World.title: Zhu Rongji, who helped turn China into a trading giant, dies at 97
World.content:
Former Chinese Premier Zhu Rongji, who spearheaded China's entry into global trade and laid the foundation for its explosive growth, has died at the age of 97.

He served in the country's second-highest office from 1998-2003 and played a leading role in securing its entry into the World Trade Organization, opening Chinese factories to the international market and drawing foreign investment.

He was one of the most important economic reformers who moved local tax powers to the central government, closed or privatised failing state firms and promoted home ownership.

Many in China remember him as a tough and pragmatic leader who delivered double-digit growth and was rarely afraid to speak his mind.

In 1998, he said China was facing "many potential crises that could erupt at any time...

"Ordinary people are discontent about us in many ways. Especially, there is corruption among officials, the gulf between rich and poor and the way some local officials act like tyrants."

He labelled rogue bankers as "half-wits" and said the dams and flood dykes lining the Yangtze River were as "flimsy and porous as tofu dregs".

Under his leadership, which helped stabilise the economy and tackle corruption, China began transforming into a manufacturing powerhouse, leaving behind its status as a Communist outsider.

Though he faced criticism because those reforms also led to 30 million lay-offs over five years, and with huge growth came more inequality.

Chinese state media describe Zhu Rongji's life as one of "revolution, struggle and brilliance".

He was born in the central province of Hunan in 1928 and earned a degree in electrical engineering before joining the civil service.

He joined the Communist Party in 1949, but was purged twice - first after criticising Mao Zedong's economic policies as "irrational" and being labelled a "rightist", and again during the Cultural Revolution.

Zhu was brought back into the fold after Mao's death, and by 1991 had risen to the role of vice-premier in charge of China's economy.

He took the role of premier seven years later.

World.title: Wisconsin result dents winning streak for Democratic Party's left wing
World.content:
David Crowley is projected to have won a primary election to become the Democratic candidate for Wisconsin governor, in a surprise comeback victory that dents a winning streak for the party's left wing.

Crowley, the more centrist candidate, won a narrow victory over Francesca Hong, according to a projection by the BBC's partner, CBS News.

Anti-establishment Democrats across the US had previously notched up victories that have rattled the party leadership in Washington. That trend did continue in another closely-watched Democratic contest in Minnesota.

But in Wisconsin, the governor's race in November will be contested by Crowley and Tom Tiffany, who easily won the equivalent Republican contest.

Crowley, the chief executive officer of the state's Milwaukee County, had a lead of less than half a percentage point over Hong with almost all votes in the Democratic contest counted, according to CBS.

In the early hours of Wednesday, he posted on X to say it was time to "get to work".

Crowley reiterated that his missions were "making life more affordable, strengthening our schools, creating good-paying jobs, and making sure opportunity reaches every corner of our state".

His new opponent Tiffany, meanwhile, currently serves as a US congressman and has the backing of US President Donald Trump.

Tiffany has also highlighted affordability issues, running on a platform that includes lowering taxes, supporting farmers and improving healthcare.

The state's political matchups are expected to be closely fought during November's midterm elections, which have also wider implications for the control of the US Congress.

World.title: Osun Election: APC chieftain urges peace, responsible political engagement
World.content:
By Dapo Akinrefon

OSOGBO — A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Osun State, Mr Olatunbosun Oyintiloye, has urged political actors and stakeholders to shun violence and promote peaceful engagement ahead of the August 15 governorship election.

Oyintiloye made the call on Wednesday while addressing journalists during an empowerment programme for informal workers at his campaign office in Ibokun, Obokun Local Government Area of the state.

He stressed that the APC remained committed to peaceful political activities and appealed to stakeholders and members of the public to promote tolerance and responsible engagement before, during and after the election.

The programme attracted informal workers, including barbers, hairdressers, fumigators, welders, textile workers, members of the National Union of Tailors and Electrical Workers, market men and women, commercial motorcyclists and members of the Nigeria Automobile Technicians Association (NATA).

Members of non-indigenous communities, including Igede, Idoma and Tiv residents from Benue State living in Obokun Local Government Area, also attended the event.

Oyintiloye said the empowerment programme was part of his efforts to support hardworking residents and strengthen grassroots participation in governance.

He urged the beneficiaries to see the initiative as an expression of his commitment to the welfare of ordinary citizens, particularly people whose livelihoods depend on their daily businesses and skills.

He also urged the participants to return to their communities and support the APC candidate, Asiwaju Munirudeen Bola Oyebamiji, in the election.

Oyintiloye said an Oyebamiji-led administration would prioritise inclusive governance, economic empowerment, skills development and improved opportunities for workers in the informal sector.

He stressed that every segment of society would be given attention under the proposed administration.

A community leader, Bishop Michael Adewale, commended the initiative, describing it as a demonstration of grassroots-oriented politics and concern for the welfare of residents.

He urged the beneficiaries to remain united and peaceful before, during and after the election, stressing that political differences should not be allowed to damage existing relationships in the communities.

Speaking on behalf of artisans and other informal workers, Mr Tijani Bello expressed appreciation for the support extended to them during the civic engagement programme.

Bello said artisans constituted a significant part of the grassroots economy and deserved access to empowerment programmes, skills development, financial support, infrastructure and better economic opportunities.

He assured the organisers that the artisans would take the message of the programme back to their communities and mobilise support for Oyebamiji and the APC.

World.title: Singer Niniola returns with new single ‘O Du Mi’ after husband’s death
World.content:
Niniola

Afro-house singer, Niniola Apata, is set to release a new single “O Du Mi”, months after the death of her husband, Michael Ndika.

The song, scheduled for release on Aug. 14 will be her first major musical project since Ndika’s passing in May 2026.

Ndika, who was the CEO of NaijaReview and also served as her manager, was married to the singer for 13 years.

Niniola shared emotional posts on social media describing her grief, including messages such as “God took him” and “My husband died,” later referring to him as her “best friend, confidant, pillar, business partner and husband”.

The singer said the new single reflects a deeply personal phase in her life, capturing themes of love, loss and emotional healing.

“Some feelings are too deep for words. So I put them in a song,” she wrote while sharing a preview of the track.

Despite the loss, she has gradually returned to public engagements, including live performances and appearances, and was recently spotted at her younger sister Teniola Apata’s album launch.

Ahead of one of her performances, Niniola said returning to music remained emotionally challenging, adding: “There are no words for a moment like this, but I know he’d want me to keep singing, to keep showing up, and to keep sharing the gift we’ve always believed in.”

Her return with “O Du Mi” is expected to mark a new phase in her career as she continues to build on her Afro-house sound.

Niniola, known for songs such as “Maradona” and “Designer,” remains one of Nigeria’s leading Afro-house artistes, blending traditional African sounds with contemporary music. (NAN)

World.title: Niger Flooding: Northern senators seek permanent solution beyond emergency response
World.content:
Flooded James Kunle Street, Light Estate, Isashi, Iba LCDA, Lagos. Some residents have abandoned their flooded homes to stay with neighbours

— Call for coordinated action by FG, state government

— Commiserate with families affected by disaster

By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — Senators from the 19 Northern states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), under the aegis of the Northern Senators Forum (NSF), have called for a permanent and coordinated solution to recurring flooding in Shiroro, Minna and other communities in Niger State.

The lawmakers said the situation required more than annual emergency responses, urging the Federal and Niger State governments to adopt long-term measures to prevent loss of lives and property.

The call followed recent flooding in parts of Minna, Chanchaga, Bosso and Shiroro Local Government Areas of the state.

In a statement issued on Wednesday, Chairman of the NSF, Senator Abdulaziz Musa Yar’Adua (APC, Katsina Central), commiserated with the government and people of Niger State, particularly families affected by the disaster.

The forum sympathised with families who lost loved ones, homes, farms, businesses and sources of livelihood, while expressing concern over the hardship faced by displaced residents.

The senators acknowledged the response of the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) and the Niger State Emergency Management Agency (NSEMA) in assessing and documenting the impact of the flooding.

However, they noted that flooding in Shiroro and other riverine communities had become a recurring problem that required both immediate intervention and long-term planning.

The forum urged the Federal and state governments, in collaboration with local authorities, to ensure prompt distribution of relief materials to verified victims and provide temporary shelters with basic healthcare and sanitation facilities.

It also called for the deployment of emergency evacuation teams and early-warning systems in flood-prone communities ahead of the peak of the rainy season.

The senators urged residents to heed safety advisories and avoid construction on waterways and other flood-prone areas.

For the long term, the forum called for the development of a Shiroro Flood Management Master Plan.

According to the senators, the plan should include a scientifically determined flood-buffer operating strategy for the Shiroro, Kainji and Jebba dams, as well as a permanent flood forecasting and early-warning system supported by trained local volunteers downstream.

The forum also proposed a comprehensive floodplain resettlement programme that would provide planned settlements, compensation and livelihood support for affected residents.

It further called for an independent technical review of dam operations, reservoir capacity and spillway performance in view of changing climate conditions, to determine how future water releases could be better managed.

The senators cited the 2025 Mokwa flooding and a 2025 vulnerability study indicating that 32 per cent of Shiroro Local Government Area was highly prone to flooding as evidence of the need for urgent action.

They said infrastructure interventions, including road and drainage repairs, should be integrated into a broader water-resource and environmental management framework addressing deforestation, inadequate drainage and unregulated development along riverbanks.

The forum assured the people of Niger State of its commitment to advocating appropriate budgetary provisions and legislative support aimed at reducing the impact of flooding and preventing avoidable disasters.

It also called on federal and state agencies, traditional and community leaders and residents to work together to protect lives and strengthen resilience against future flooding.

The senators prayed for comfort for bereaved families, strength for displaced residents and wisdom for authorities working to find lasting solutions to the recurring flooding.

World.title: Osun Poll: Police, military, INEC don’t belong to APC — Atiku
World.content:
Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar

By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA — Former Vice President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, yesterday warned the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), security agencies and the Federal Government against using state institutions to tilt the Osun governorship election in favour of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

Atiku described the poll as a critical test of Nigeria’s democratic credentials, warning that the scale and posture of security deployment around the election risked making a civil democratic exercise look like a military operation.

Speaking at the ADC National Youth Leadership Summit in Abuja, he said the conduct of the Osun election would send a strong signal about Nigeria’s readiness to deliver credible elections ahead of the next general election.

“Elections are civil engagements, not military operations. Ballot papers are not bullets. Voters are not enemy combatants. Opposition members are not insurgents,” he said.

Atiku questioned why such overwhelming security capacity was being deployed for an election when terrorists, kidnappers and bandits continue to attack communities and kill Nigerians.

He also cautioned INEC against any attempt to frustrate voters or compromise the integrity of the process through technical failures, unexplained delays or opaque handling of results.

The former vice president demanded the timely arrival of electoral materials, unhindered voting, honest counting and transparent transmission of results.

“The police belong to Nigeria. The military belongs to Nigeria. INEC belongs to the Nigerian people. None of them belongs to the APC,” he declared.

Atiku said the eyes of Nigerians and the international community would be on Osun, urging all institutions involved in the election to allow voters to freely determine the outcome.

“The world is watching Osun. Nigerians are watching. History is taking notes. Let the people vote. Let every vote count. And let the will of the people prevail,” Atiku said.

The ADC presidential candidate also returned to the controversy surrounding the Chicago State University certificate President Bola Tinubu submitted to INEC, demanding clarification of what he described as discrepancies in documents linked to the certificate.

Atiku said the certificate submitted to INEC reportedly bears June 22, 1979, while another document produced in connection with Chicago State University records bears June 27, 1979. He also pointed to reported differences in the signatures and description of the degree.

He questioned the appearance on documents dated 1979 of names or signatures associated with university officials whose tenures reportedly began years later, asking whether replacement certificates were subsequently produced and, if so, who authorised them.

Atiku cited Section 137(1)(j) of the Constitution, which provides for disqualification where a presidential candidate has presented a forged certificate to INEC, arguing that the precise document submitted to the electoral commission should be authenticated.

“Who produced the certificate Tinubu submitted to INEC? When was it produced? Who authorised it? Why does it differ from the other version, and does Chicago State University authenticate the exact document submitted to INEC?” he asked.

He argued that the standard expected of an ordinary Nigerian seeking employment should not be lowered for someone seeking the country’s highest political office.

“If a young Nigerian would be required to explain such discrepancies before getting an ordinary job, why should the man seeking Nigeria’s highest job be exempt from the same standard?” Atiku asked.

On youth participation, Atiku pledged that at least 30 per cent of legislative candidates under his political programme would be below 40, with a significant number below 30.

He urged young Nigerians to turn their frustration into organised political participation rather than stopping at social media activism.

“Anger is not an organisation. A hashtag is not an organisation,” Atiku said, urging young Nigerians to move beyond online expressions of frustration and take an active role in shaping the country’s political future

World.title: Osun election: Police arrest 4 over alleged attempted murder, firearms possession
World.content:
File image.

The Police Command in Osun has arrested four suspects over alleged attempted murder and possession of firearms in Modakeke, Ife East Local Government Area of the state.

The spokesperson for the command, DSP Abiodun Ojelabi, made this known in a statement on Wednesday.

Ojelabi said the suspects were arrested over alleged conspiracy, attempted murder, assault occasioning harm, and unlawful possession of prohibited firearms.

“The arrest followed a petition written and addressed to the Commissioner of Police concerning the alleged offences,” he said.

He explained that the four suspects – two male and two female were arrested on Sunday at about 2.00p.m by police operatives.

He said during the search conducted at the suspects’ residences, two firearms were recovered.

“One cut-to-size locally made firearm was recovered from the shop of one of the female suspects while one pump-action firearm was recovered from the residence of the other female suspect,” he said.

Ojelabi said the suspects were in police custody and assisting the police in the ongoing investigation, while efforts were ongoing to apprehend others at large.

In another development, Ojelabi said operatives of the Violent Crime Response Unit (VCRU) of the command arrested six suspected members of an unlawful society in Osun State Polytechnic, Iree.

He said the suspects were apprehended following information received that some hoodlums invaded the campus with dangerous weapons and injured two students on the school premises.

Ojelabi said during interrogation, two of the suspects confessed to being members of the ‘Aye Confraternity’.

He said the investigation is ongoing and that all the suspects would be charged in court after the investigation is completed.

He said the command was committed to protecting lives and property and maintaining peace and security.

Ojelabi encouraged residents to continue to provide credible and timely information to the police to prevent crime.

World.title: Road projects cause over 5,000 fibre cuts in six months — NCC
World.content:
Maida

By Progress Godfrey, Abuja

The Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) has recorded more than 5,000 fibre-optic cable cuts across the country in the first six months of 2026, largely caused by road construction, excavation and related civil works.

Speaking at a stakeholders’ workshop on the protection of fibre-optic cables during road construction and rehabilitation activities, in Abuja yesterday, Executive Vice-Chairman of the NCC, Dr Aminu Maida, said inadequate coordination among stakeholders was responsible for many of the incidents.

Maida said the recurring damage was disrupting essential digital services and increasing costs for telecommunications operators, businesses and citizens.

“The scale is significant. In the first six months of this year alone, over 5,000 fibre-cut incidents were recorded from road construction, excavation and related civil works,” he said.

He explained that the impact of damaged fibre cables extended beyond telecoms operators, affecting banking, government services, education, healthcare, commerce, security and emergency communications.

Maida recalled that fibre cuts in late February 2024, including those caused by road construction, led to an almost network-wide disruption for one telecommunications operator, leaving millions of subscribers unable to make calls, send messages or access the internet for several hours.

Speaking further, the NCC boss said, “Our interests are aligned; what has too often been missing is a dependable system of early coordination.”

On government’s response, Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, Engr Nadungu Gagare, represented by the Director of Telecoms and Postal Services, Stanley Musa, described the protection of fibre infrastructure as a shared national responsibility.

Gagare said recurring fibre cuts could undermine broadband expansion by disrupting essential services, raising operational costs and potentially discouraging investment in the digital sector.

He noted that the ministry was working with stakeholders to strengthen compliance with right-of-way regulations and improve coordination around telecommunications infrastructure.

Meanwhile, Director, Critical National Assets and Infrastructure Protection at the Office of the National Security Adviser, Air Vice Marshal Effiom Enebong Ewa, stressed that damage to fibre infrastructure had implications beyond technical faults.

Ewa emphasised that damaged fibre cables could affect governance, economic productivity, public services and the lives of Nigerians, noting that fibre-optic infrastructure had been designated as Critical National Information Infrastructure.

He urged contractors, government institutions, telecommunications operators and other stakeholders to comply with established protocols during construction and maintenance activities.

World.title: Ebonyi Assembly passes laws regulating house rent, agent fees, scrap trade
World.content:
By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki

ABAKALIKI — The Ebonyi State House of Assembly has passed a bill seeking to regulate the sale and handling of metal and electrical scraps, house rents and estate agency fees in the state.

The bill, which was passed during plenary at the House of Assembly Complex, Nkaliki Road, was presided over by the Speaker, Rt. Hon. Moses Ije Odunwa.

The law, which takes effect from August 11, 2026, is to be cited as the Ebonyi State Sale of Scraps, House Rent and Agent Fees Regulation Law, 2026.

The legislation seeks to regulate the sale, possession, transportation and disposal of metal and electrical scraps, standardise rents and curb excessive agency fees charged by both professionals and non-professionals.

Under the law, no person shall buy, sell, possess for sale, transport or dispose of metal or electrical scraps except as a licensed dealer in accordance with regulations made under the law.

An offender is liable to imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years or a fine of not more than N500,000.

The law also provides that any landlord who obtains an order for possession of an accommodation through fraud, misrepresentation or concealment of a material fact commits an offence and is liable to two years’ imprisonment.

It further stipulates that estate agents’ fees shall not exceed two per cent of the gross sum of the transaction.

From the commencement of the law, the standard rent prescribed by the governor for different categories of accommodation shall apply, and landlords are prohibited from charging above the prescribed standard rent.

To promote transparency and professionalism in property transactions, the law requires all estate agents operating within the capital city to register with the Ministry of Capital City Development.

The Leader of the House, Hon. Kingsley Ogbonna Ikoro, said the legislation was designed to curb the vandalism of public and private property, environmental degradation and exploitative practices in the housing sector.

Contributing to the debate, Hon. Victor Nwoke, representing Abakaliki North; Hon. Nwodo Aloysius Nwodo, representing Ebonyi North-West; Hon. Oluchukwu Ukie Ezeali, representing Afikpo East; Hon. Friday Ogbuewu, representing Ezza South; and Hon. Celestine Ogba, representing Onicha East, described the legislation as timely and necessary.

They said it would help address the increasing cases of scrap theft and arbitrary rent increases in the state.

In his remarks after the passage, the Speaker said the activities of some scrap dealers had contributed to damage to public and private property and other challenges in society.

He said the new law would promote public safety and restore sanity to property transactions in the state.

The bill was exhaustively considered by the Committee of the Whole, with members examining it page by page and making corrections to grammatical and drafting errors.

Following the consideration, the bill was unanimously passed by the lawmakers.

World.title: PDP denies PVC hoarding allegation in Ebonyi
World.content:
— alleges threats, planned arrest of members

By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki

ABAKALIKI — The Ebonyi State chapter of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has denied allegations that its members are involved in the illegal procurement or hoarding of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs).

The party described the allegation as a campaign against its members and alleged that it could be used as a basis for intimidation, harassment and arrest of its supporters and officials.

The State Publicity Secretary and spokesperson of the PDP in Ebonyi, Prince Darlington Peter Onwe, stated this on Wednesday at a press conference in Abakaliki.

Onwe alleged that the development came amid heightened political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He also referred to previous comments attributed to the state governor, Francis Nwifuru, regarding the PDP and other opposition parties in the state, saying the party had expressed its concerns to relevant authorities.

“Our party is a law-abiding political organisation, and at no time has it contemplated, authorised or condoned any conduct capable of violating the Electoral Act 2026, the guidelines of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), or any other extant law of the Federal Republic of Nigeria,” Onwe said.

He said the PDP rejected any attempt to associate its members with alleged unlawful dealings involving PVCs.

The party spokesperson further expressed concern over what he described as possible actions against its members, saying such measures, if undertaken without due process, could infringe on their constitutional rights.

He urged security and electoral institutions, including the Police, National Security Adviser, Department of State Services (DSS), INEC and human rights bodies, to monitor developments in the state and ensure that political activities were conducted in accordance with the law.

Onwe also referred to an earlier incident at Ikwuator, Idembia, in Ezza South Local Government Area, where he alleged that political thugs disrupted a PDP event organised to receive a former APC member into the party.

He alleged that journalists covering the event were also affected during the incident.

The PDP spokesperson said the party had placed its members, structures and stakeholders on alert and would pursue lawful channels to address any alleged infringement of their rights.

He reiterated the party’s commitment to peaceful and constitutional political activities and urged the state government and APC leadership to focus on issue-based engagement ahead of the 2027 elections.

As of the time of filing this report, the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Ebonyi State had not responded to the allegations.

World.title: FG Committed to Healthcare Delivery Nationwide, Says Permanent Secretary
World.content:
Felix Omoh-Asun in Benin

The Federal Government is committed to reshaping health delivery system in the country through innovative and funding of healthcare facilities across the nation.

The Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Daju Kachollom, disclosed this in Benin Wednesday during the inauguration of some projects at the University of Benin Teaching Hospital (UBTH) to mark one year anniversary of Prof. Idia Ize-Iyamu as the Chief Medical Director (CMD).

The permanent secretary, represented by the Medical Director of the National Orthopedic Hospital, Benin, Dr. Philip Ugbodaga, urged support for the President Bola Tinubu presidency to continue to energize the health sector for the good of all.

She affirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to strengthening healthcare delivery under President Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda.

She praised the CMD, the University of Benin Teaching Hospital (UBTH), Benin, for actualizing the mandate that the ministry and the president has given her to help to transform and bring to the teeming masses the goodies of democracy.

Kachollom, who performed the unveiling of the Special Investigation Unit (SIU), among other projects, commended the CMD of the UBTH for her remarkable achievements in her first year in office.

She praised the CMD for her prudent management, visionary leadership, and efforts to improve infrastructure and clinical services, describing her as a beacon of hope and a trailblazer as the hospital’s first female chief medic.

Kachollom said the achievements recorded within 365 days demonstrated her commitment to transforming the hospital and improving healthcare delivery.

She pledged to submit a comprehensive report, supported by photographic evidence, to the Minister of Health for further commendation.

Facilities inspected include renovated security facilities, a 65-bed Accident and Emergency complex, an expanded mortuary upgraded from 72 to 460 chambers, a multi-faith centre, premium and regular renal dialysis units, a child-friendly paediatric clinic, a revitalised oxygen plant, a geriatric ward, a 160-slice CT scan, a special investigation unit, dental and oncology centres and improved theatre facilities.

Prof. Ize-Iyamu, the CMD, said that the extensive infrastructural and service upgrades undertaken by her administration is to improve patient care and experiences.

The CMD said the projects were driven by the need to provide patients with safe, dignified and world-class healthcare services.

The CMD stressed that UBTH remains a one-stop tertiary healthcare institution with specialist services covering neurosurgery, oncology, dentistry, eye care, renal services and other complex medical needs.

She reaffirmed the hospital’s commitment to providing quality healthcare to all patients irrespective of age, gender, tribe, religion or social status, noting that sickness knows no boundaries.

Ize-Iyamu also announced plans to extend its impact to underserved communities through its comprehensive health centre at Udo, where 5,000 people will receive free medical services, including cataract surgery and other treatments.

A new dental centre equipped with two dental chairs, mobile units and X-ray facilities will also be inaugurated at the centre.

She thanked the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, development partners, donors, staff and other stakeholders for their support, assuring them that UBTH would continue to improve its facilities and patient experience while remaining open to the public.

World.title: Foundation Provides Free Medical Outreach in Kwara, Targets over 3,000 Residents
World.content:
Hammed Shittu in Ilorin

As part of effort to take healthcare delivery to the people of the grassroots in Kwara State, a non governmental organisation, Eniobanke Foundation for Humanity has provided free medical outreach to over 3,000 residents of Ilorin on different kinds of ailments.

The outreach which commenced at Emir’s palace, Ilorin on Wednesday will come to an end on Friday at Tanke area of Ilorin, the state capital.

Speaking with newsmen in Ilorin on the sideline of the event held at Ilorin Emir’s palace, the Director of Programme of the foundation, Mr. Quadri AbdulSamad said that,

“Foundation is borne out of passion for service to

humanity and to give back to the society, with over 3,000 residents will be benefiting at the three days free medical outreach in Ilorin.

“It is also due to the foundation’s love for the people so as to boost their socio well being and to bring them closer to health care delivery and it is holding inconjuction with the Federal Medical Center, Markudi in Benue State.

“It is a free health outreach programme that would assist the residents of Ilorin to have access to free healthcare delivery without hindrance.

“The event will take three days and end at Tanke area of Ilorin with no fewer than 3, 000 residents of Ilorin having access to free medical service”.

Abdulsamad explained further that, the outreach was part of the mandate of the foundation to bring quality medical attention to the less privileged people in the society.

He said that, the outreach would assist the people suffering from different kinds of ailments to have access to medical attention from the qualified medical personnel recruited for the exercise.

AbdulSamad stated that, the exercise would also allow the medical personnel to embark on the testing of the beneficiaries and provide drugs free of charge to them while those that cannot be treated there would be referred to the appropriate medical centers.

He also said about seven states of the country, Kwara, Oyo, Ogun, Oyo, Edo, Cross River, Delta and Plateau would also benefit from the outreach is inconjuction with the Federal Medical Center, Markudi, Benue State.

Also speaking, the Medical Coordinator ot the outreach, Mr. Ibrahim Saddiq, said that, “We are basically to give back to the society through provision of free medical care to the beneficiaries.

“And we are going run test on HIV, High blood pressure, eyes, sugar among others..

“The beneficiaries would be allowed to see the Medical personnel recruited for the exercise.

“After the medical treatment, the beneficiaries would be provided with free drugs and those that are above the medical personnel would be referred to specialist hospital for proper attention”.

Most of the beneficiaries who spoke with newsmen lauded the humanitarian gestures of the foundation.

They said that the free medical outreach would reduce current burden of many households due to the present economic crunches in the country.

World.title: Don’t Stop Food Import Now, Fix Insecurity First, TUC tells FG
World.content:
*Seeks pay rise for workers

*Demands urgent passage of state police bill

Onyebuchi Ezigbo in Abuja

The Trade Union Congress, (TUC) has urged the Federal Government not to suspend food importation, warning it will push up price of rice and other staples to unaffordable levels.

The union called on the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to consider revaluing the naira to N900-N1000 to a dollar, saying the current N1,380/$ rate is fuelling inflation and impacting negatively on workers’ earnings.

TUC however said it endorses government’s push for state police and the adoption of the NLNG privatization model for refineries.

TUC President-General, Comrade Festus Osifo, who spoke at a Press Conference in Abuja on Tuesday said that importation should continue until insecurity is tackled and farmers return to farms.

He used the opportunity to highlight the union’s position on the economy, security, labour, and governance issues

Responding to plans by the federal government to review the policy lifting of ban on importation of rice and other stable foods, TUC president said that the union is in support of sustaining food import untill such a time when food production improves with farmers having unfettered access to farmlands.

Osifo recalled that in early 2024, TUC submitted a 15-point demand to government, including measures to address food security.

He said insecurity had prevented farmers from accessing their farms, forcing prices up.

“At that time we told government to look for food all over the world, because it is when people see food to eat that they can go to work, that they can go to school,” he said.

He noted that the policy to grant licences for food importation helped to crash prices.

“We don’t want a bag of rice to go back to N100,000 or N120,000. Even where it is today, we still believe it is relatively high.,” he said.

The TUC leader said food importation should only be stopped “only and only if farmers can go back to farms” and the supply gap is closed. “When supply is limited and demand remains constant or increases, price is going to increase,” he said.

In addition, Osifo called on CBN to revalue the naira to N900-N1000 to a dollar, saying the current N1,380/$ rate is fuelling inflation without reflecting in workers’ wages.

Osifo also called on the Central Bank of Nigeria to revalue the naira to around N900 to N1000 to a dollar, arguing that the current rate of about N1,380/$ is still too high and is fuelling inflation.

He said while macroeconomic indicators have stabilised, “it has not dovetailed llllinto the microeconomy” where workers and traders feel the impact daily.

“The only people that devaluation helps is actually the workers, because every other item reflects the naira component. But what never reflects devaluation is the earnings of Nigerian workers,” he argued.

“We strongly believe that the fair value of our naira using purchasing power parity could be somewhere around 900 naira, maximum 1,000 naira to a dollar. CBN has what it takes to manage the exchange rate to about 1,000 naira,” he said.

TUC further said it endorses state police and the adoption of the NLNG privatization model for refineries.

He also said the union is in support of legalizing State Police, adding that the federal government should fast track the passage of Bill to help reduce insecurity in the country.

He dismissed fears of abuse of the state police by those in the helm of affairs at subnational, said that such concerns by few politicians should not negate its importance as a tool to address insecurity crisis across the country.

On refineries, TUC endorsed the NNPC plan to adopt the NLNG model — reduce government equity to 49% and bring in technical private investors with 51% — instead of outright sale.

The TUC commended the Director General of DSS , Oluwatosin Ajayi, for arrests and prosecution of bandits and terrorists.

He also hailed government’s salary increase of 50-80 percent for military personnel, saying that it should extend similar gesture to all public sector workers.

Regarding the ongoing strike by aviation workers, TUC said it supports the move by the affiliate union to get the management of airlines to allow their workers to unionize.

World.title: BBNaija S11: What ‘The Gambit’ Voting Reveals About Sentiment Over Strategy
World.content:
When Big Brother introduced “The Gambit” in the first week of Season 11, it gave viewers a rather unusual choice. One male and one female housemate would be guaranteed a place until the finale, but permanently barred from winning the ₦160 million grand prize. On paper, it was a strategic decision. Viewers could identify potential threats, protect housemates they felt were valuable to the show, or simply keep certain people around while taking away their shot at the money.

But what happened with the votes revealed something we already know too well: sometimes, Nigerians vote with their feelings first. Flora became the female Gambit with 29% of the votes, while Aikou took the male slot with 9%. And the two choices were interesting for different reasons.

Flora’s selection was driven largely by her appeal as a housemate. Viewers had already seen her boldness, energy and potential to bring drama, so for many, the thinking was simply: “She’ll make the show interesting, let’s keep her around.” Some may not have fully considered what making her a Gambit actually meant. As a Gambit, Flora was guaranteed a place until the finale but could no longer win the ₦160 million grand prize. So, in the end, the vote was less about making her the winner and more about wanting her to stay.

In other words, the appeal was not necessarily, “Flora should win.” It was more like, “I want Flora to still be here.” Here, sentiment did the one thing sentiment is supposed to do: it showed up as votes.

Aikou’s case complicates that picture. From the beginning, he had the “brains” thing going for him; calm, analytical, thoughtful and carrying that Professor-like energy. Certain viewers liked him for that; they saw someone intelligent and different from the usual loud personalities that often dominate reality television. But his numbers were also shaped by something closer to actual strategy: some viewers openly said they saw him as a threat and wanted him locked out of the prize while still in the house. That is a calculated move, not a sentimental one, and it sat alongside the viewers who just liked “the Professor” and wanted him around. Aikou’s vote, in other words, was a genuine mix of sentiment and strategy in a way Flora’s wasn’t.

Then came the first real eviction, and the picture flipped. Martins and Mercedes were the first to leave, with Martins receiving just 1.63% of the votes and Mercedes 2.29%, while Keivo narrowly survived with 2.92%.

Martins’ exit was fairly straightforward. A good number of viewers simply did not see enough of him. He was considered “low-impact” or “boring” by many, and there was not much emotional attachment pushing people to fight for his place in the house. Nobody was really making the argument that he had to stay because he was some dangerous strategic player.

Sometimes, you don’t get evicted because people actively dislike you. You get evicted because people don’t care enough to save you.

Mercedes was a completely different situation, and this is the case that actually reveals the gap. People clearly enjoyed Mercedes. Her energy, her boldness and her ability to create moments made her one of the more noticeable housemates. From the birthday lap dance for Martins to the arguments and her generally unfiltered personality, she was giving viewers something to talk about.

So when she left, the reaction was, understandably, “Wait, how?” People complained that one of the people actually bringing energy into the house had gone too soon. There was shock, frustration and the usual social media questioning of whether viewers were even voting properly.

But then you have to ask: if people really liked Mercedes that much, why didn’t enough of that liking translate into votes?

Many people loudly support housemates on social media without actually opening the MyDStv or MyGOtv app to vote. That small extra step can be the difference between a housemate who is widely loved online and one who actually receives enough votes to stay in the house. This is where Mercedes becomes the clearest evidence in the piece: not that Nigerians vote on feeling instead of strategy, but that feeling and voting are two separate acts, and a lot of us stop at the first one.

Flora shows sentiment successfully becoming votes. Mercedes shows sentiment failing to become votes. Put together, they suggest the real story isn’t “Nigerians vote with their hearts”, it’s that having a feeling about someone and being willing to act on it are not the same thing, and the size of that gap is what actually decides outcomes.

Most viewers are not sitting down to calculate who the biggest threat is, who should remain eligible for the ₦160 million grand prize or who will matter three weeks from now. Sometimes, the calculation is much simpler: “I like this person. I enjoy watching them. I want them to stay.” And to be honest, there is nothing strange about that. It is a reality show; people watch to be entertained, and emotional connection is part of what makes them care enough to vote.

That does not mean strategy is always better. Big Brother’s house run like a chess game would be boring. Personality, entertainment and emotional connection are part of what makes the show worth watching. The problem is when liking someone quietly substitutes for actually doing something about it, and we only recognise the gap after the fact.

The Gambit and the first eviction have offered a small but revealing mirror: what we feel about someone and what we are actually willing to do for them are not always the same thing. Perhaps the real question is not whether Nigerians vote with their hearts or their heads, but whether we notice the gap between feeling something and acting on it before the eviction, not after.

World.title: Terroso Moves to Strengthen Nigeria’s Cold Chain Infrastructure
World.content:
Iyke Bede

Terroso Agriculture, a subsidiary of Terroso Group, has joined the Global Cold Chain Alliance (GCCA), in a move aimed at strengthening Nigeria’s cold chain infrastructure and reducing post-harvest losses across the agricultural value chain.

The partnership will enable the company to leverage global expertise, industry standards, research and strategic partnerships in developing modern cold storage facilities, temperature-controlled logistics and preservation technologies.

Nigeria continues to lose a significant proportion of its agricultural produce due to inadequate cold chain infrastructure, which affects food security, farmer incomes, and the competitiveness of the agricultural sector.

Through its membership in the GCCA, Terroso Agriculture said it plans to support investments and partnerships that will improve the preservation and transportation of perishable agricultural products from farms to markets.

The GCCA represents companies involved in temperature-controlled warehousing, logistics and transportation globally, promoting practices aimed at preserving the quality and safety of perishable products while advancing innovation, operational efficiency and sustainability in cold chain operations.

Speaking on the development, Chief Executive Officer, Terroso Group, Opeoluwa Runsewe, said the partnership would support the company’s efforts to strengthen Nigeria’s food system through improved cold chain infrastructure.

“By working with GCCA, government and industry partners, we aim to reduce post-harvest losses, improve food security, strengthen supply chains, increase farmer incomes and build a technology-driven cold chain ecosystem that enhances Nigeria’s agricultural competitiveness and drives sustainable growth across Africa.”

Welcoming Terroso Group to the alliance, Manager, Marketing and Communications, GCCA, Serena Moriarty, said the company’s focus on cold chain infrastructure aligned with the organisation’s objective of strengthening temperature-controlled supply chains globally.

Senior Vice President, Global Market Engagement, GCCA, Adam Thocher, said the company’s focus on food preservation and supply chain infrastructure reflected the leadership needed to strengthen cold chain networks.

“We are excited to welcome Terroso Group into the GCCA community. Their vision for transforming food preservation and supply chain infrastructure reflects the kind of leadership required to strengthen global cold chain networks.”

Terroso Agriculture said it would continue to invest in cold chain infrastructure, logistics and agricultural value chains as part of efforts to improve food preservation, enhance supply chain efficiency and support long-term food security in Nigeria and across Africa.

World.title: UNICEF Seeks N1.2bn Nutrition Funding for Katsina
World.content:
Francis Sardauna in Katsina

The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) has called on the Katsina State Government to increase its investment in child nutrition by allocating N1.2 billion to the Child Nutrition Fund in the 2027 budget.

The Chief of UNICEF Field Office, Kano, Mr. Shafeeq Ur-Rehman, made the request when he led a delegation on a courtesy visit to Katsina State Governor, Dikko Umaru Radda at the Government House weekend.

Ur-Rehman said the proposed N1.2 billion contribution by the state would be matched by UNICEF to strengthen interventions aimed at tackling malnutrition among children and women in the state.

He said the funding would support the procurement of Multiple Micronutrient Supplements for pregnant women, as well as Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Food (RUTF) and other essential commodities for children under five suffering from severe wasting.

He commended the Radda administration for its consistent contribution to the Child Nutrition Fund, describing Katsina as one of the few states in Nigeria that had sustained its financial commitment to the fund over the years.

The UNICEF official stressed the need for increased investment in nutrition, particularly as the state continues to confront the challenge of child malnutrition.

He also disclosed that Katsina State was participating in a global pilot of the revised World Health Organisation (WHO) guidelines for the prevention and management of severe wasting in children.

Nigeria, he said, was one of only five countries selected globally for the pilot, which is currently being implemented in 10 local government areas of Katsina State.

Ur-Rehman said: “Katsina’s participation in this pilot is important because the lessons from here will not only contribute to nutrition programming in Nigeria but will also provide useful evidence for the global response to child malnutrition.”

He further commended Governor Radda for making Katsina the first and only state in Nigeria so far to appropriate N270 million for the implementation of a SMART Nutrition Survey.

He said the survey would generate reliable and timely nutrition data to identify vulnerable communities, guide resource allocation and strengthen interventions targeting women and children.

Ur-Rehman reaffirmed UNICEF’s readiness to support the state in conducting the Rapid SMART/SMART+ Nutrition Survey, stressing that evidence-based data remained critical to effectively addressing malnutrition.

Responding, Governor Radda pledged to include UNICEF’s additional N1.2 billion funding request in the state’s 2027 budget “despite the financial constraints facing the government”.

“We are not doing it for you; we are doing it for our people,” the governor said, assuring UNICEF of the state government’s continued commitment to interventions capable of producing measurable improvements in the lives of residents.

Radda said his administration had approved the release of N500 million as counterpart funding for the Child Nutrition Fund and described the investment as part of efforts to improve nutrition, healthcare and other development indicators in the state.

He said the collaboration between Katsina State and UNICEF had yielded encouraging results, particularly in the treatment of child malnutrition, adding that the number of children requiring treatment at stabilisation centres and outpatient treatment sites had begun to decline.

World.title: INEC Includes SDP Candidate, Ajala, On Ballot for Osun Guber Poll
World.content:
Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has announced that the candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) for the Osun State governorship election, Dr. Francis Ajala and his running mate, Faseke Oladipo, have been added to the ballot for the election on Saturday.

INEC National Commissioner and Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee, Mohammed Haruna, in a statement explained that the action was taken in compliance with the judgment of the Federal High Court, Abuja, delivered on July 22, 2026 in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/344/2026, between SDP and Ajala on the one hand and INEC on the other.

He recalled that the court had ordered the commission to forthwith recognise, accept, upload, process and publish the name and particulars of Ajala as the candidate of SDP.

Haruna noted: “Consequently, the ballot papers for the election, scheduled to hold on Saturday, 15th August 2026, are being reproduced to reflect this addition, bringing to 15, the total number of political parties contesting the election.

“The result sheets for the election are also being reproduced alongside the ballot papers to reflect the inclusion of the SDP candidate.”

The commission informed the public that the reproduced ballot papers would arrive in Osun State on Thursday, August 13, 2026, and would, same day, be moved to local government area offices across the state, in line with its standard distribution procedure ahead of the election.

The commission assured political parties, candidates and the general public of its commitment to conducting a free, fair and credible election in Osun State.

World.title: Accord Appeals to EU for Urgent Intervention Over Rising Tension Ahead of Osun Poll
World.content:
* Peter Obi condemns threat-laden remarks, urges retraction, peaceful election

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

Accord Party on Wednesday appealed to the European Union (EU) for urgent diplomatic intervention to de-escalate rising political tension in Osun State, condemn alleged electoral violence and intimidation, and help ensure a free, fair, credible, transparent and peaceful governorship election scheduled for Saturday.

The appeal was contained in a letter dated August 12, 2026, and addressed to the Ambassador and Head of the EU Delegation to Nigeria and ECOWAS, Gautier Migot, by Accord National Chairman, Chief Maxwell Mgbudem.

The party said the August 15 election was particularly significant as the last major off-cycle governorship election before the 2027 general election, warning that its conduct and outcome would have far-reaching implications for public confidence in Nigeria’s democratic institutions and electoral process.

Accord alleged that the political atmosphere in Osun had become increasingly tense amid reports of violence, intimidation, arrests, harassment and what it described as the deployment of state institutions and security agencies in ways capable of undermining political competition.

According to the party, at least 29 people had reportedly lost their lives, while several others sustained gunshot injuries in incidents linked to the political environment in the state.

It further alleged that more than 60 of its members and supporters had been arrested and detained in Abuja and Nasarawa State under circumstances it said required urgent clarification and independent scrutiny.

The party also raised concerns over the reported searches of residences of senior Osun State Government officials and the arrest and detention of some officials, including the Secretary to the State Government, as well as the reported freezing of the state government’s bank accounts by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC).

Although the affected officials were later released and the accounts reportedly unfrozen following public concerns and presidential intervention, Accord said the incidents had heightened apprehension over the perceived use of state institutions in the political environment.

The party stressed that it did not seek to obstruct legitimate law-enforcement or anti-corruption activities, but urged that such powers be exercised impartially, transparently and in accordance with due process, particularly during an election period.

Accord’s appeal to the EU came against the backdrop of its demand for the immediate arrest and prosecution of Senator Francis Adenigba Fadahunsi, representing Osun East Senatorial District, over a viral video in which the party alleged that he incited supporters to kill Accord Party members and supporters in Ijesaland.

The party described the reported remarks as outrageous and reprehensible, arguing that they had further escalated political tension only days before the governorship poll.

It called on the Inspector-General of Police (IGP) and the Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS) to investigate the senator’s alleged conduct and take appropriate action, while urging security agencies to protect all political actors and citizens.

The party also appealed for the immediate release of its members allegedly detained in Abuja and Nasarawa, insisting that their continued detention could prevent them from participating in Saturday’s election.

The party urged the EU, the United States, United Kingdom, African Union (AU) and ECOWAS to closely monitor developments in Osun and condemn actions capable of undermining democratic participation.

In a related intervention, the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate for the 2027 election, Peter Obi, has condemned what he described as the “inflammatory comments and threat-laden rhetoric” attributed to Fadahunsi.

Obi demanded an immediate retraction and apology, stressing that political leaders had a constitutional and moral responsibility to promote peace, democratic norms and unity.

He urged security agencies to monitor inflammatory statements and guarantee equal protection for voters, election officials and citizens before, during and after the poll.

According to Obi, the democratic mandate belongs to the people and no individual, irrespective of political office or status, should attempt to influence the electorate through fear, intimidation or coercion.

In its appeal, Accord urged the EU to use its diplomatic influence to encourage political parties, candidates and their supporters to reject violence, inflammatory rhetoric and intimidation.

It also called for strict neutrality and professionalism by security agencies and public institutions, while urging the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to discharge its responsibilities independently, impartially and transparently.

The party further sought credible domestic and international observation, accountability for perpetrators of political violence and respect for lawful mechanisms for resolving electoral disputes.

Accord said it was not asking the EU to take sides, but to support democratic principles, political pluralism, rule of law and the right of Osun voters to freely choose their leaders.

It warned that the election represented a critical test of Nigeria’s democratic credentials, insisting that “preventive diplomacy” was needed before violence or institutional distrust could cause irreversible damage.

The party said a peaceful and credible election would strengthen confidence in Nigeria’s democracy ahead of 2027, while any perception of violence, intimidation or institutional manipulation could deepen public distrust.

Accord concluded by urging all stakeholders to allow the people of Osun State to determine their political future through a peaceful, transparent and credible electoral process.

World.title: The R100 grocery list that makes supper for a whole week
World.content:
In any other economy, you might be tempted to find a high-paying job to avoid the mid-month blues.

That may not be possible in this economy.

Instead, if you want your salary to last until month-end, you can rely on a trusty mid-month hack.



Spend R100 on this grocery list and get supper for an entire week.

R100 Buys a Grocery List that Makes Enough supper for a Week

This list can help you when funds are low. But it’s also scientifically proven to contain all the nutrients you need.

The three ingredients, when combined, should give you enough meals for the week.

Buy a starch. On a budget, you have two options: Maize meal and rice. Choose whichever suits your taste. This list relies on rice.

You can buy a 2-kilogram bag of parboiled long-grain white rice and have it cooked in 30 minutes.

Most weeks, supermarkets will have one brand of 2kg rice on promotion.



If your budget is strict, maize meal might be a better option.

It’s slightly more expensive to buy at R35 for 2.5kg, but you can get breakfast and supper from it.

Choose your protein. You really only have one option: pulses, also known as legumes.

Lentils will be the best choice because they’re key to the scientific process.

To get a tasty lentil dish, you need sauce. Stick to the rule: If you aren’t sneezing, it’s not seasoned.

Use any meaty marinade in your fridge or meat-flavoured spice in your cupboard.

With enough meaty flavour, you won’t get any earthy notes common when cooking lentils.

Choose your vegetable. To create a complete dietary profile, choose butternut or carrots.

Butternut offers you the most value for money.

You can get a pocket weighing roughly 6 kilograms for R40.

Carrots, on the other hand, cost R20 for 1 kilogram.

You can also buy an onion, one or two tomatoes, and some green pepper to flavour your lentils, should you make any savings.

If you fill a bowl with 50% rice, 25% lentils and 25% butternut, you should be able to get 21 meals from these ingredients.

You could comfortably feed two people supper with this list.

But families may need to get a second bag of lentils to last for a week of suppers.

Item Price Whole Lentils 500g R28 Butternut Pocket R40 Rice R32 Total R100

Where to Splurge

If you have more than R100 and want some actual meat in the meal, you have two options: chicken soup packs or pork.

Chicken soup packs are sold at Pick ‘n Pay and Shoprite for R55 per kilogram.

Pork sells for R60 per kilogram at most supermarkets.

The Science Behind the Complete Meal

Beyond being affordable, this meal is scientifically proven to contain every nutrient you need.

According to a daily nutritional calculator, the average South African* should be getting the following nutrients:

Nutrient Requirement One Plate of R100 Supper Protein 26 g 4.3 g Fibre 25 g 11 g Vitamin A 700 μg 488 μg Vitamin B6 1.3 mg 0.5 mg Vitamin C 45 mg 14 mg Iron 18 mg 4.3 mg Magnesium 310 mg 77 mg Potassium 2 800 mg 631 mg Zinc 8 mg 2.1 mg

*The average South African is based on data from Statistics South Africa.

A 350-gram bowl of lentils, rice, and butternut can get you roughly 25% of these nutrient requirements.

This is based on Eat This Much: cooked and unsalted rice (175g), lentils (87.5g), and butternut (87.5g).

There are also other health benefits to this cost-effective meal.

Data from ScienceDirect shows that lentils are good for your gut and help with digestion and inflammation. Butternut can help lower or control cholesterol.

Now, should you fall on hard times, you know what to buy with only R100.

World.title: This week’s snowfall was epic, but doesn’t match ‘Snowtember’
World.content:
This week's Eastern Cape snow warning was serious, but South Africa's real snow record dates back to September 2024: Image ChatGPT

This week’s Orange Level 6 warning cut off parts of the Eastern Cape and made for genuinely dramatic headlines.

But is it an Eastern Cape snow record?

No.



South Africa’s real benchmark for severe snow dates back to September 2024. This week doesn’t come close.

What actually happened this week

SAWS issued an Orange Level 6 disruptive snow warning for the Eastern Cape’s Emalahleni, Sakhisizwe, Senqu, Elundini and Matatiele municipalities, warning of major traffic disruption and communities becoming temporarily inaccessible.

It was serious enough that a SAWS forecaster later confirmed the system itself, while significant, “was not out of the ordinary” for a South African winter.

The Eastern Cape snow record actually belongs to September 2024

In September 2024, a system nicknamed “Snowtember” triggered a SAWS Level 8 warning. It shut the N3 Toll Route completely between Estcourt in KwaZulu-Natal and Harrismith in the Free State for close to two days.

Motorists were stranded for more than 14 hours in freezing conditions, with reports of at least one death linked to exposure.

Five provinces were affected, including the Eastern Cape, and it took a full multi-agency rescue and recovery operation to clear stranded vehicles from Van Reenen’s Pass.



Why this Eastern Cape snow record comparison matters

It’s easy for a dramatic week to feel like “the worst we’ve seen,” especially when it’s playing out in your own backyard. But stacking this week’s system against 2024’s shows just how much more severe South African winters can get.

I think it’s worth remembering these events when they happen, because it puts each new cold front into real perspective rather than just headline shock value. Hey, I for one wish I got the opportunity to see the snow in 2024.

Do you remember where you were during the 2024 “Snowtember” chaos?

Let us know in the comments below, Mzansi …

Is it snowing in your area? If so, please send your photos to info@thesouthafrican.com

World.title: Transfer news: Pirates links swirl as Polokwane coach speaks on Matuludi
World.content:
Polokwane City coach Willy Moloto has addressed the absence of star defender Thabang Matuludi from the matchday squad amid continued transfer speculation.

The 26-year-old right-back has attracted interest from several top clubs, including Orlando Pirates and Mamelodi Sundowns, in recent months. He was heavily linked with a move away from Polokwane City during the current transfer window.

However, Moloto insists Matuludi’s absence has nothing to do with the ongoing speculation surrounding his future.



“There’s no such thing. Every time people don’t see a player, they start with the talk,” Moloto told FARPost.

The Polokwane coach explained that Matuludi has been dealing with minor knocks after being involved with Bafana Bafana at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

“Remember, Matuludi was also with Bafana Bafana [at the 2026 FIFA World Cup], and he picked up some knocks in training.

“The team has also been doing well, so sometimes there is no need to change.”

Matuludi sidelined but…

“If it’s not broken, why fix it? He will get his chance—there are a lot of games.

“Let’s give the youngster [Surprise Manthosi] a chance. He did well even though he had some mistakes in the first half [in the league tie against Stellenbosch on Tuesday],” he said.



Despite Moloto playing down concerns over Matuludi’s absence, the defender continues to be linked with a move to one of the country’s biggest clubs.

Orlando Pirates are reportedly among the favourites to secure his services, particularly after the Buccaneers released two right-backs in July.

Who should Pirates sign next?

World.title: Two leading UK hotels, one judge, and the R22-billion lenders no rule book governs
World.content:
A United Kingdom high court judge has frozen the sale of two Hilton branded hotels, in London and York, while the courts decide whether one of Britain’s fastest growing unregulated lenders was entitled to take control of the company behind them.

Administrators were appointed in June 2026 over Project Q Senior Ltd – which holds the 297 room Hampton by Hilton near Waterloo station and the DoubleTree by Hilton in York – after the group borrowed more than £94 million (R2.1 billion) from Cohort Lendco II, a lending vehicle of Park Lane-based Cohort Capital.

The company’s new owner, hotel investor Boutros El Khoury, has applied to the high court to remove the administrators. The court has fast tracked the case: a trial of up to three days from 1 October, in front of a high court judge, with witnesses on both sides to be cross examined, and until judgment the administrators may not agree to sell any asset of the company.



Cohort Capital: Background

Cohort Capital, founded in 2019, says it has deployed more than £1.7 billion and has partnered with major international investment funds on its largest transactions.

It was founded by chief executive Matt Thame, and its directors include Bal Sohal, the chairman of Birmingham developer SevenCapital and co-owner of Cynergy Bank, who sits on the board of Cohort Capital and on each of its lending vehicles, including the one that lent to the hotels.

Cohort is what the UK regulator, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), calls an “Annex 1” firm, a label most people will never have met because it comes from a schedule buried in the UK’s money-laundering regulations. What it means in plain terms is this: around 1,200 lenders, brokers and leasing companies must put their names on an FCA register so their money laundering checks can be inspected, and that is the full extent of the regulator’s grip.

They are not authorised or supervised the way a bank is. No rules govern how they treat the businesses they lend to. Their borrowers cannot complain to the Financial Ombudsman. And when a loan goes wrong, the lender’s powers run on the contract alone, which can move from a missed payment to control of an entire business within days, with no regulator watching.

That gap in the rules is now under pressure. The FCA warned in March about risks at Annex 1 lenders, and, as the Financial Times reported this week, the £1.3 billion collapse of Market Financial Solutions has prompted the regulator to demand information about business models and financial crime risks from around 900 more of these firms.

There is no suggestion that Cohort Capital, the administrators or S&W Partners have done anything wrong; the October hearing will decide only whether the conditions for the administrators’ appointment were met.



But the case will put the machinery of unregulated enforcement, how fast it moves and who checks it, in front of a judge in open court, and lenders, borrowers and the regulator will all be reading the judgment.

Approached for comment by The South African, El Khoury said: “We have asked the high court to determine whether the appointment of administrators over the company was valid.

“The court has certified the matter for an expedited hearing in October and has ordered that no binding sale of any of the company’s assets may be agreed before judgment. The hotels continue to trade normally, and our priority is their staff and guests. As the matter is before the court, we will not be commenting further.”

Both hotels are trading normally.

World.title: Can hair transplantation be performed on afro-textured hair?
World.content:
Hair transplantation can absolutely be performed on afro-textured hair, but the surgical approach has to change. Image: Supplied

Curly, coily and tightly coiled hair follicles do not grow the way straight hair does, and this difference matters far more in a hair transplant setting than most patients realise.

The short answer is yes, hair transplantation can absolutely be performed on afro-textured hair, but the surgical approach has to change to account for how these follicles sit beneath the skin.

Patients researching afro hair transplant options often come across this question early, usually after being told by a local clinic that their hair type is “too risky” or “not a good candidate” for FUE.



In most cases, that assessment says more about the clinic’s experience level than about the patient’s actual eligibility.

Afro-textured hair grows in a curved path, not a straight one.

Above the scalp, the curl is visible to the eye. Below the scalp, the follicle itself often bends, sometimes at a sharp angle, before reaching the bulb where the hair actually grows from.

This subcutaneous curvature is the single biggest reason why afro hair transplantation has a reputation for being harder to perform.

Understanding the Structure of Afro-Textured Hair

Hair type is generally classified on a scale from straight (type 1) to tightly coiled (type 4), and most patients seeking afro hair restoration fall into the type 3 or type 4 range.

The follicle wall in these hair types tends to be thinner on one side than the other, which is part of what causes the curl pattern in the first place.



It also means the follicle can be more fragile during extraction if the surgeon does not adjust technique accordingly. Learn more about Afro-textured hair.

Hair Type Follicle Path Extraction Difficulty Straight (Type 1-2) Vertical, minimal curve Lower Wavy/Curly (Type 3) Moderate curve beneath skin Moderate Coily/Afro (Type 4) Sharp curve, sometimes spiral Higher, requires specialized technique

Why Afro Hair Transplantation Requires a Different Surgical Approach

Standard FUE punches are designed around a straight extraction path.

When that same tool is used on a curved follicle, the punch can sever the follicle partway down, a problem known as transection.

A transected graft either fails to grow or grows in a weakened, thinner state, which is why transection rates are watched so closely in afro hair cases.

Follicle Curvature and Extraction Challenges

Surgeons working with afro-textured hair typically extract at a shallower angle and rely more heavily on tactile feedback than visual cues alone, since the curve of the follicle cannot always be predicted just by looking at the hair above the skin.

This slows the extraction process considerably compared to straight-hair cases, but it also protects graft integrity.

Graft Survival and Transection Risk

Donor area management becomes especially important here.

Afro hair patients often have naturally lower graft density in the donor zone compared to Caucasian or Asian hair types, so preserving every viable follicle matters more.

A surgeon who treats a high volume of afro hair cases usually tracks transection rates closely and adjusts punch size and angle based on what the individual patient’s follicles look like under magnification.

Techniques Used for Afro-Textured Hair Restoration

Clinics experienced in afro-textured hair restoration typically apply adapted FUE protocols alongside microscopic donor analysis and sapphire punches as small as 0.6-0.7mm, which can reduce tissue trauma during extraction regardless of curl pattern, though the angle and depth of entry are adjusted case by case for coily hair.

FUE Adaptations for Curly Follicles

Rather than following a fixed protocol, surgeons examine the donor area under magnification before deciding on punch size and extraction angle.

Some grafts in a single session may require different handling than others, depending on how tightly the follicle curls beneath the surface.

Doctor-Led Precision in Extraction and Implantation

Because curved follicles leave less room for error, channel opening and the more delicate extraction stages are typically handled directly by the physician rather than delegated entirely to technicians.

This is part of a broader donor-preservation philosophy: the goal is not just to place grafts, but to protect the limited donor supply that afro hair patients often start with.

What Determines Candidacy for Afro Hair Transplant

Candidacy depends on several factors working together rather than any single measurement.

Donor density, curl tightness, scalp elasticity, and the pattern of hair loss all play a role in the surgical plan.

Traction alopecia, common among patients who have worn tight protective styles for years, sometimes affects the hairline and temple areas differently than typical male or female pattern loss, which changes how grafts are distributed across the recipient area.

Donor area density and curl tightness under magnification

Scalp laxity and skin condition

Pattern and cause of hair loss, including traction-related thinning

Realistic expectations about density given the donor supply available

Recovery and Results Expectations
