World.title: Everything you need to know as Australia hosts Bangladesh in the Top End
World.content:
Australia is hosting Bangladesh in a rare Test series this August, as winter cricket hits the Top End.

The two teams will play two Tests, the first of which gets underway in Darwin on August 13 at Marrara Stadium.

The second starts on August 22 in Mackay, where Harrup Park will become the 12th ground to host a men's Test match in Australia.

You can listen to live coverage of both Tests on the ABC Listen App, or follow the ABC Sport live blog.

'Nowhere to hide' or free swing?: ABC Cricket Podcast

It is the first time in 23 years that Bangladesh will tour Australia for a Test series.

Here's everything you need to know.

When does Australia play Bangladesh?

The first Test gets underway on Thursday, August 13, with the first session starting at 10am ACST in Darwin, NT.

That means the start time is 10:30am AEST (Queensland, New South Wales, ACT, Victoria and Tasmania), 10:00am in South Australia and the Northern Territory, and 8:30am in Western Australia.

The second Test starts on Saturday, August 22, with the first ball again set to be bowled 10:00am AEST in Mackay, Queensland.

That is 10am in Queensland, New South Wales, ACT, Victoria and Tasmania, 9:30am in South Australia and the Northern Territory, and 8am in Western Australia.

Each Test is scheduled for five days.

Where are the Tests being played?

Australia played South Africa at Marrara Stadium last year in a T20 international. (Getty Images: Cricket Australia/Albert Perez)

August is not normally cricket season in Australia, but officials are taking advantage of the dry season in the north to take these matches to the tropics, with Darwin and Mackay hosting the Test matches.

Darwin's Marrara Oval will host just its third ever men's Test match and first since Sri Lanka visited in July 2004.

Australia have a 100 per cent winning record in Tests in Darwin, winning by an innings and 132 runs against Bangladesh in 2003, following that up with a 149-run victory against Sri Lanka the year after.

Australia has also played four ODIs in Darwin, all against Bangladesh and all resulting in emphatic victories.

In T20Is it's a slightly different story though, with South Africa sharing the spoils across two matches at the venue last year.

Mackay's Harrup Park has never hosted a men's Test match before and will become the 12th venue in Australia to do so.

Harrup Park in Mackay will become the 12th ground to host a men's Test match in Australia. (Getty Images: Albert Perez)

The ground did host a youth Test match last year between Australia and India's under 19 sides, a low-scoring match won by India by seven wickets.

There have been three ODIs at the ground, two of them involving Australia. Again, South Africa were the opponents in 2025 and, again, the spoils were shared.

The only other ODI took place during the 1992 Cricket World Cup between India and Sri Lanka.

Given that Mackay averages 313.2 millimetres of rain in February — the wettest month on average across the year for the city — it's perhaps not a surprise that rain meant that the match was abandoned after just two balls were bowled.

That was even after a helicopter hovered above the pitch in an attempt to dry it out.

Australia's women have played three ODIs (in 2021) and two T20Is (in 2024) at the ground, winning all but one game.

Who is playing?

Pat Cummins returns for Australia's first Test of the season. (Getty Images: Cricket Australia/Mark Brake)

Australia has named a strong squad, with front-line bowlers Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon all returning following their injury lay offs.

Such impressive bowling depth has seen Michael Neser miss out, the luckless Queenslander then suffering a hamstring injury in any case that will keep him out of contention.

It is, essentially, a full strength team, something Bangladesh skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto, is pretty impressed about.

"I personally liked the fact that they have chosen their full-strength team," he said earlier this month in an interview with ESPN Cricinfo.

"They are not taking us lightly. I think our team has earned this respect."

Najmul Hossain Shanto will lead Bangladesh in Australia. (Getty Images: Sameera Peiris)

Disappointingly for Bangladesh, they come into the series missing two key weapons in lightning-fast seamer Nahid Rana, who has been ruled out due to a left-side strain, and Shoriful Islam, who has a hurt hamstring.

Then, key spin bowler Taijul Islam suffered a blow to the hand in the warm up game and did not bowl at all in the second innings.

The 23-year-old Rana is one of the form bowlers in world cricket, capable of delivering the ball at speeds in excess of 150km/h. He has already taken 44 wickets in international cricket this year — the most by any bowler — at an average of 18.31.

On a positive note, Litton Das recovered from a calf injury he picked up during the home ODI series against Australia in June.

Batting is a problem for the tourists though — chief selector Habibul Bashar said the selection of 33-year-old lefty Soumya Sarkar was as a result of "a bit of desperation". Hardly a ringing endorsement for a man who has not played Test cricket since 2021.

Australia Squad Bangladesh Squad Pat Cummins (c) Najmul Hossain Shanto (c) Scott Boland Amite Hasan (wk) Alex Carey (wk) Ebadot Hossain Cameron Green Hasan Mahmud Josh Hazlewood Jaker Ali (wk) Travis Head Khaled Ahmed Josh Inglis (wk) Litton Das (wk) Marnus Labuschagne Mehidy Hasan Miraz Nathan Lyon Mominul Haque Steven Smith Musfik Hasan Mitchell Starc Mushfiqur Rahim (wk) Jake Weatherald Shadman Islam Beau Webster Soumya Sarkar Taijul Islam Tanzid Hasan Taskin Ahmed

Jake Weatherald, the first Northern Territorian to play a Test for Australia, was watching on in the crowd the last time the Australians played in Darwin.

He is a great chance to start on his home ground after a solid spell in the County Championship with Leicestershire, where he scored 483 runs at an average of 60.37, including scoring an unbeaten 104 against Glamorgan in Cardiff.

What form are Bangladesh in?

Bangladesh have only lost one of their last five Test matches. (Getty Images: Sameera Peiris)

Bangladesh come into this Test series off the back of a pretty decent run, having lost just one of their last five matches in the format.

Two thumping victories at home against Ireland in November 2025 were backed up by a hugely impressive 2-0 series victory against Pakistan in May this year.

That wasn't bad.

Now for the things that have been pretty poor.

A one off Test against Zimbabwe at the Harare Sports Club resulted in a calamitous defeat by an innings and 85 runs.

If that was bad, then the absolute thrashing the Cricket Australia XI delivered last week was even worse, the tourists bowled out for just 54 in their second dig as the CA XI won by an innings and 38 runs.

If it wasn't for Mehidy Hasan Miraz's unbeaten century in the first innings, rescuing his side from 6-110, who knows how bad the score would have looked as Corey Rocchiccioli took 6-83 in that first innings and Campbell Thompson took 8-25 in the second.

What is Bangladesh's record against Australia?

Jason Gillespie's stunning double century will go down in the annals as one of the best ever night watchman displays. (Getty Images: Hamish Blair)

Bangladesh have only ever played against Australia six times in their Test history — they've only played fewer Tests against Ireland (3) and Afghanistan (2) which, given Bangladesh have been a Test-playing nation since 2000, is a damning inditement on Australia's commitment to playing the minnows.

Somewhat surprisingly then, Bangladesh does have a Test victory against Australia to their name and, it was their most recent series in 2017.

Bangladesh claimed a stunning 20-run victory in Mirpur, with Shakib Al Hasan claiming player of the match honours after scoring a 133-ball 84 in the first innings and taking 5-85 with the ball in the final innings.

Australia got revenge in Chattogram, winning by seven wickets as Nathan Lyon took 7-94 and 6-60, while David Warner scored a brilliant, six-hour, 234-ball 123 in the first innings.

Australia's best ever batting performance in Chattogram though came 11 years before that, when night watchman Jason Gillespie scored a stunning unbeaten 201 to help Australia claim victory by an innings and 80 runs.

The first Test of that series in Fatullah had been won by the far more tense margin of three wickets, with Ricky Ponting's grinding 118 not out helping the Aussies over the line.

Bangladesh have never beaten Australia in Australia though, losing both their 2003 Tests by over an innings, in matches that took place in Darwin and Cairns.

Tech.title: Google aims for influencers with the Pixel 11 Creator Suite
Tech.content:
Google knows creators are a big audience. The occupation is growing fast, and landing some influential names could be a major turning point for the Pixel’s market share. This year, Google is building features directly into its new Pixel lineup that it says can help creators record, organize, edit, and publish content faster and more efficiently than they could on other devices.

Creator Suite is a new mode built into the Pixel 11’s camera app. The suite comes with features like a teleprompter, vocal enhancer, external microphone levels, and social media frame guides, which Google thinks will entice users who want to start building channels and have limited resources.

“ We really wanted to do something for those folks who are creating on their phones to make it easier to do that, make it faster to publish, fewer retakes, easier organization, and just streamline that workflow,” Isaac Reynolds, who leads the Pixel camera team, tells The Verge.

Reynolds says there is a massive gap between the top and bottom of the creator market, where the biggest creators have teams and resources, but the “hundreds of thousands of creators” in the bottom of the market need more accessible ways to make content.

“ They’re striving to put out content weekly or daily, even when they have full-time jobs,” Reynolds says. “They’ve got money coming in, it’s very enticing, but it’s not the replacement for their work yet.”

A frame guide with a cutout where the buttons show up on TikTok.

The arrival of TikTok has fundamentally reshaped what it means to be an influencer or a content creator, and the barrier to entry to do that work is lower than ever; all you need to do is film a selfie video. Over the last five or so years, the creator industry has both professionalized and de-professionalized: Influencers are signed to talent agencies and retain professional management, but there’s also been an explosion of cheap and fast content that is not tied to a specific personality — all that matters is whether it’s being served up to audiences. AI slop is everywhere. Follower count is increasingly irrelevant, and making content for the internet is, in theory, an attainable job for anyone, including people with other full-time jobs. Google recognizes that and wants those legions of people to use its phone.

Google has tried to court this demographic before, at least indirectly: Last year, it tapped Alex Cooper, host of the popular celebrity interview podcast Call Her Daddy, to make Google ads and post selfies on Instagram with the Pixel (she also promoted photo editing features at Made By Google last year). The partnership touted how Google’s ecosystem would help Cooper’s business as a content creator — scripting videos, shooting content, and keeping her team organized. Google now wants to reach the individuals who are pumping out content by themselves with just a phone.

Photography by David Imel / The Verge

Tech.title: The 7 biggest announcements of Google’s Pixel 11 launch
Tech.content:
is a news writer covering all things consumer tech. Stevie started out at Laptop Mag writing news and reviews on hardware, gaming, and AI.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Google is hosting a Pixel launch event on Wednesday night where it will show off its latest lineup of devices. But you don’t have to wait until then for all the news: We were able to check out the devices ahead of the event and take a look at everything Google’s unveiling, including the latest Pixel phones, new health features on the Pixel Watch 5, and more.

Google will be livestreaming the event on Wednesday at 6PM ET / 3PM PT. But if you aren’t able to watch along yourself, you can catch up on all of the highlights from Wednesday’s Pixel launch below.

Photo: David Imel / The Verge

Google refreshed its line of Pixel phones, starting with the Pixel 11. The design didn’t change drastically compared to the Pixel 10, although it now comes in a few new colors, including a lilac-like frost, hibiscus pink, and pistachio green, along with obsidian black. It runs on Google’s new Tensor G6 chip, which Google claims offers 25 percent faster web browsing and 15 percent faster app loading. Google also says its battery lasts over 30 hours and supports 25 percent faster wireless charging than the Pixel 10.

The Pixel 11 also features an upgraded camera and a camera bump that’s over 40 percent thinner than the Pixel 10’s. It includes 48MP wide, 13MP ultra-wide, and 10.8MP 5x telephoto lenses on the back and a 10.5MP selfie camera on the front. Google says the 48MP wide lens has 56 percent more light sensitivity and the 5x telephoto lens supports up to 30x Super Zoom.

Unfortunately, the Pixel 11 also got a $100 price bump — it now starts at $899, but the base configuration has 256GB of storage and 12GB of RAM, rather than the 128GB of storage in the Pixel 10’s starting configuration. It launches on August 20th.

Photo: David Imel / The Verge

Google’s Pixel 11 Pro and 11 Pro XL include a new feature in the camera bar called HiLight, which is an LED indicator light for things like Gemini interactions and incoming calls from favorite contacts. Google says the little LED will get more capabilities down the line, like signaling message notifications from frequent contacts.

The Pixel 11 Pro also features an upgraded display that maxes out at 3,600 nits. Inside, it has Google’s Tensor G6 chip like the base Pixel 11. The camera includes a new 48MP telephoto lens with up to 120x Pro Zoom and a new 50MP wide lens, along with a 48MP ultra-wide lens and a 42MP selfie camera. According to Google, it offers over 30 hours of battery life and over 29 percent faster wireless charging compared to the Pixel 10 Pro / Pro XL.

The Pixel 11 Pro starts at $1,099 with 256GB of storage and 12GB of RAM while the Pro XL starts at $1,299 with the same specs. The 512GB and 1TB storage options include 16GB of RAM. The Pro and Pro XL are both available in four colors: canyon, fog, olive, and matte obsidian.

Photo: David Imel / The Verge

Google says the Pixel 11 Pro Fold features the thinnest bezels ever on a Fold and claims it’s three times as durable as the Pixel 10 Pro Fold, with IP68 water and dust resistance and a back material that’s “designed to be nearly impossible to crack.”

The Fold’s displays are 20 percent brighter than last year’s model and the inner display goes up to 3,600 nits of brightness like the Pixel 11 Pro / Pro XL. It also runs on Google’s Tensor G6 chip and offers up to 24 hours of battery life. The camera includes a new 48MP wide lens plus a 10.5MP ultra-wide lens and a 10.8MP telephoto lens with up to 30x Super Zoom.

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold costs $100 more than last year’s model, starting at $1,899 for a base configuration with 256GB of storage and 16GB of RAM and two color options: olive and black.

Photo: David Imel / The Verge

In addition to hardware upgrades, Google’s also introducing some new features for taking photos and videos across its new lineup of phones. The Camera app has a new capture mode called Magic Capture that can pull photos and clips out of video recordings.

There are also Camera Looks, which offers customizable, stylized photo presets that change how your phone processes the photo, rather than simply applying a filter. The various Looks include styles like minimal, editorial, and “digi,” which mimics digital cameras. The Pixel 11 Pro also has a new Pro Stable Video feature Google says can record at up to 8K.

A new Creator tab in the Camera app has a “Creator Suite” with tools for trimming and reordering videos, an onscreen teleprompter, and improved Speech Enhancement.

Photo by Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge

The new Pixel Watch 5 might look essentially the same as the previous version, but it includes some major new software features. Breathing Emergency Detection, a follow-up to last year’s Loss of Pulse feature, can trigger an emergency call if the watch detects a significant, sustained drop in blood oxygen saturation (SpO2). The Pixel Watch 5 can also track nightly sleep breathing quality and sum up the data in monthly reports. Starting in September, Google’s also introducing Blood Pressure Trends and Insulin Resistance Trends.

The Pixel Watch 5 has some new workout features, as well, like AI-generated strength training plans and the option to track reps directly from your watch. Google claims it includes the “most accurate GPS route tracking for exercise, outperforming Apple Watch Ultra 3 and Garmin Fenix 8 Pro.”

Unfortunately, this year’s Pixel Watch is a little pricier — it got a $50 price bump and now starts at $399. It’s available in two sizes, 45mm and 41mm, and four colors: black, white, olive green, and pink. There’s also a Steph Curry special edition that costs $579 and launches a bit later on September 3rd.

Photo: David Imel / The Verge

Google’s taking on Apple’s AirTag with the Pixel Tag, its own item tracker, launching on November 11th for $29 individually or $99 for a pack of four. It’s oblong rather than round, measuring 1.1 inches by 1.8 inches (the AirTag is 1.26 inches across). The tracker is IP67 water and dust resistant and Google says its replaceable CR2032 coin cell battery lasts over a year.

Photo by Andru Marino / The Verge

Google is releasing the two-year-old Pixel Buds Pro 2 in a new olive green color on August 12th, which matches the olive Pixel 11 Pro and Pro Fold. In September, Google’s also rolling out a firmware update for the Buds Pro 2 that’s supposed to improve the earbuds’ Active Noise Cancellation.

Tech.title: Google’s Pixel 11 series pairs a little new hardware with a lot of new software
Tech.content:
is a technology reporter who has been covering the industry since 2007. He co-hosts the Waveform podcast with MKBHD. A former engineer, he now specializes in topics like computational photography and social media protocols.

When I first picked up the Pixel 11 Pro this week, it was clear to me that this was one of those refinement years — at least when it comes to hardware. Aesthetically, the phones are as beautiful as ever, with Google’s signature camera bar and bright, colorful backing glass. There are small updates, like a single piece of glass covering the camera bar and the all-new HiLight ambient LED on the Pros. But this year, the Pixel is all about quality of life and software improvements.

After weeks of teasers, Google has finally formally announced the Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro XL, and Pixel 11 Pro Fold. The phones are all shipping next week, on August 20th, and Google is holding a splashy event the evening of August 12th to show off the devices. Ahead of that, we had a chance to take a first look at everything that’s coming up.

Pixel 11

The standard Pixel 11 gets some bold colors this year.

Let’s start with the bad news up front: All of these phones are $100 more expensive than last year’s. Google has killed off the 128GB base storage option this year, which means the Pixel 11 now starts at $899 for a 256GB model. All storage tiers still come with 12GB of RAM, but the higher entry price is no doubt driven by RAMageddon, which has been increasing costs across the industry.

If you can look past the price, you’ll find a refined version of last year’s phone that looks and feels a bit more premium. The camera bar is now made of a singular piece of glass and is over 40 percent thinner. If you use it with one of Google’s cases, the bar will become completely flush. (This gives you three different camera bar thickness options on the Pixel line now, which only get thicker the more premium you go.)

The camera bump difference between the Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro.

The cameras have been upgraded, too. On the Pixel 11, the 48MP wide is quoted with 56 percent more light gathering capability from its new 1/1.56-inch sensor, and the 5x telephoto lens can now digitally zoom up to 30x, which Google says is enabled by the new image signal processor in the Tensor G6 chipset. And considering the new Tensor G6 chip is said to be up to 20 percent more efficient, Google is quoting up to 30-plus hours of battery life across the lineup.

Perhaps the most interesting update to me is the new Camera Looks feature. You can think of this similarly to the film recipes on Fujifilm cameras, presenting users with stylized presets that can be customized to their liking.

Editorial Camera Look. Minimal Camera Look.

What makes Camera Looks so interesting, though, is instead of just being a filter on top of the preprocessed Pixel photo, the phone will process the photo completely differently at the sensor level depending on which settings you choose, potentially using less frame stacking and sharpening to deliver the photo you actually want. During my briefing at least, this really delivered. The Natural mode does an amazing job of lowering the sharpness and contrast and making the photos look much more true to life, and I’m excited to take it for a proper spin later. If you want to learn more about this, check out my dedicated article where I spoke with Pixel camera lead Isaac Reynolds.

Another new feature inside the camera is Magic Capture. This is a camera mode alongside the photo and video modes that creates a sort of hybrid mashup of the two, where the phone will automatically pick out short clips and images you can share. During my hands-on time this feature didn’t work great, only giving me one small clip and one photo from a roughly 15-second recording, but I believe it’s meant for longer clips at things like kids’ birthday parties. We’ll have to test this in the field once we have more time with the device.

Magic Capture. Creator Suite.

Google is also adding a new Creator Suite inside the camera, which gives you access to tools like social media framing guides, speech enhancement, a teleprompter, and automatic folder structures for video. I was surprised to see this so deeply integrated into the camera itself, and it’s clear Google is going after a new audience and hoping to make the Pixel the best phone for small creators.

The phones also all feature Qi2.2 — an upgrade from Qi2 last year. Google says this offers 25 percent faster wireless charging of up to 25W, an upgrade from the 15W max the Pixel 10 offered. However, many users reported seeing a maximum wireless charge rate of only 5W with the Pixel 10 when using older chargers, so hopefully the problem is fixed this year.

The Pixel 11 will come in purple, green, black, and an extremely hot magenta.

Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL

The Pixel 11 Pro in blue.

The 11 Pro and Pro XL are where things get a little more interesting this year. Like the standard Pixel 11, they start at 256GB of storage and 12GB of RAM (down from 16GB last year), which starts at $1,099. If you’re a power user, you can still get 16GB of RAM if you buy the 512GB or 1TB models.

You’re definitely getting more with the Pro models this year, though. The display on the Pixel 11 Pro gets up to a super bright 3,600 nits, which Google says is the brightest display ever on a smartphone. This isn’t a massive difference from the 3,300-nit peak brightness from last year, but it’s something for your money.

The Pixel 11 Pro beside a Pixel Watch 5. The new camera bar is all glass.

The main camera sensor on the Pixel 11 Pro has been improved, with a new 50MP model that Google says uses less power and should perform better in the 1x-to-5x zoom range. There’s also a new 48MP telephoto lens with a larger 1/1.95-inch sensor that delivers a quoted 30 percent improvement in light sensitivity. And just like the standard Pixel 11, the 11 Pro has a further zoom range, now extending up to 120x, which Google says is enabled by the ISP in Tensor G6.

On the Pro phones, Google has also substantially sped up Night Sight, offering up to 4.5x faster low-light image capture, though Google tells me on average it’s about 3x faster than last year. This is still a pretty substantial improvement, and Reynolds told me the idea was to optimize Night Sight for handheld capture. “You can still capture for up to four minutes if you want all the light,” he tells me, “but it’s really optimized for those awkward moments where you have to tell someone to hold still for a little too long.”

The HiLight LED replaces the old temperature sensor.

The flashiest feature (pun intended) of the new Pro phones is the HiLight feature. Pixel 11 Pro and Pro Fold phones now feature an RGB LED ring where the temperature sensor used to be on the right side of the camera bar. When you’re talking to Gemini, the LED will glow blue as it listens and responds to you. Separately, you can set favorite contacts to glow when they call you through the default Phone app or WhatsApp. Google is marketing the feature as a way to be more present in your everyday life, but it doesn’t feel particularly useful to me yet considering its use is so limited. Google says more functionality is coming in the future, but right now, this doesn’t feel like a reason to buy the phone.

The Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL will come in olive, light blue, and a striking orange-ish “canyon” color, all with glossy side rails. There’s also a black option, which this year has matte side rails, unlike all the other Pro devices.

Pixel 11 Pro Fold

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold in olive.

Finally, there’s the Pixel 11 Pro Fold. Google is calling it the most durable Pixel Fold yet, with a new composite back material that Google says is nearly impossible to crack. This, alongside a thicker inner ultra-thin glass display, contributes to Google’s “3x more durable” claim compared to last year.

The inner bezels have also been reduced, making it Google’s thinnest Fold bezels ever, and the peak brightness matches the Pixel 11 Pro at 3,600 nits. The 11 Pro Fold is also inheriting the new 48MP main sensor from the Pixel 11 for a quoted 56 percent improved light sensitivity compared to last year, and it gets Qi2.2 for up to 20 percent faster wireless charging.

The 11 Pro Fold starts at 16GB of RAM standard with 256GB of storage, comes in olive and black, and starts at $1,899 — also a $100 price jump over last year.

Photography by David Imel / The Verge

Tech.title: Google is making the Pixel cameras better by making them worse
Tech.content:
is a technology reporter who has been covering the industry since 2007. He co-hosts the Waveform podcast with MKBHD. A former engineer, he now specializes in topics like computational photography and social media protocols.

If you look at a photo taken by a smartphone today, it’s hard to find much that’s technically wrong. Faces are bright and visible. The skies are pristine and blue. Even at night, scenes are well lit and noise-free. If the physical limitations of a tiny camera are what you’re trying to solve for, you could probably label smartphone photography a mostly solved problem.

But in our current moment, the photos people are drawn to are not flawless — and that’s created a real problem for the people making smartphone cameras. “The gap between what two random people want from their camera is growing dramatically,” says Isaac Reynolds, who leads the Pixel camera team at Google. Some people want a perfectly optimized photo, Reynolds says. “But there’s a growing number of people who want something that they feel is more authentic or traditional, by their definition.”

That’s what Reynolds and the Pixel team are setting out to solve with Camera Looks, a total rethink of how the camera captures and styles an image on the Pixel 11 series. The phones include a new suite of processing tools aimed at giving people much more control over the camera’s output. At first glance, they look a lot like filters, with names like Black Tie, Classic, and most strikingly, Digi, in reference to the growing trend of buying cheap digital cameras from the early aughts. But unlike a filter, which generally applies editing tweaks after the processing happens, Camera Looks is changing how image data is processed at the sensor level.

Editorial Camera Look. Minimal Camera Look.

“The pipeline spans the entire system,” Reynolds says. “It’s inside HDR Plus. It’s inside the processing engine. It’s inside the camera app as well in how we make certain decisions about auto exposure and integration time and number of frames packaged and captured.”

In the last decade or so, smartphone cameras have been engineered to do battle with the limitations of physics using what’s known as “computational photography.” Too dark? Night mode uses multi-frame image stacking to brighten the photo without adding too much noise. Need to zoom in but don’t have a telephoto lens? An on-device model can artificially create data it expects to be in your photo. Too small of a sensor for natural blur? Phones can use subject segmentation to recognize objects, cut out the subject, and emulate depth of field.

The result has been crisp, clear photos — and also a lot of (mostly younger) consumers carrying around old iPhones and cheap point-and-shoots from the early aughts to get a simpler, less processed, and (to their eye) better look.

“If you are looking for a minimal look … we simply don’t do the processing at all.”

The Pixel 11’s new Camera Looks feature is Google’s response to this growing trend. And to solve it, the Pixel team is allowing users to dial back how much processing happens when they snap a shot. Some of the Pixel’s Camera Looks will merge fewer frames together, leaving the highlights a bit blown out instead of compressing them to a midtone. Some of them won’t apply as much sharpening and will instead leave the image softer on the edges. You could argue that these new photos are technically “worse” — with reduced detail and dynamic range — but the result should be a photo closer to what any given user actually wants. This is a completely different way of thinking about computational photography, using tools to optimize for style instead of for technical perfection.

Until now, the Pixel camera pipeline has done the same type of processing for every user, and any edits to match their preferred style had to be made after the fact. But when an image is already fully processed, you’re stuck with the data and artifacts caused by that processing. “Once you’ve processed it that way, you can’t do less. If there was a merge artifact, that is baked in. It’s irreversible,” Reynolds says. With the Pixel 11, “we bring it a lot earlier, and that way if you are looking for a minimal look, which is minimally processed, we simply don’t do the processing at all.”

Various Camera Looks from the Pixel 11

This, I think, is the most Google way to handle this change in camera mindset I could have imagined. In order to keep people from being too confused about technical jargon like tone compression or frame merging, Google is intelligently making processing decisions for you based on style selections most users can understand — and more importantly, can see. Reynolds tells me that there were long debates inside the camera team for just how many sliders users should have access to, and they landed on more than you’d probably expect.

“ There are so many in there that I actually had to have an escalation meeting with my PM and my UX team about how many controls we were allowed to put in there,” Reynolds says. “There’s a lot of controls that photographers say are critical to have. We had a lot of trouble cutting it down.” For every Camera Look, you’ll get a set of six or more different levers, like contrast, warmth, tint, and saturation. And some Looks, like the black-and-white look Black Tie, will give you extra options, like red, green, and blue filters, which darken certain frequencies of light on black-and-white film.

This is notably different from the way Apple is currently thinking about cameras on the iPhone. Since the iPhone 13, Apple has included “Photographic Styles” in its camera — a series of presets that users can dial in through only two settings, tone and color (brightness/contrast and saturation). Google gives you access to these settings, too, but you’re also getting access to computational settings like sharpness and grain, which can more dramatically tune the look of your image before you shoot.

The Camera Looks interface

Giving users this much control over their images is a major step change for Google. The last time I had an in-depth conversation with Reynolds was in 2019 for the launch of the Pixel 4. At the time, Google’s priority was not to make a camera at all, but rather a magic box, where the user would simply point, shoot, and get what it considered the “perfect” image.

Simplification is not the priority this year. Now, it’s about choice. But Reynolds is still convinced that Google’s default settings are correct for most people, so the first option in the list of Looks is called “Original” — the experience Google has delivered for years. “ We do user studies with large N counts that are global, where we very, very carefully control the demographics, and we’re very confident that the original Pixel look is the right look,” he says. “We have no debate about that.”

The ‘Digi’ Look is going to be popular

There are simpler looks that only make subtle changes from Original, like Natural, Shadows and Vanilla, but there are also much more stylized Looks, like Editorial, Classic, and Velvet. If I were a betting man, I would say Google styled these directly after Fujifilm’s popular film simulations, but Reynolds won’t quite go that far. “These are film-inspired,” he tells me. “I would not say that these are film copies. I wouldn’t want to tell you that this is supposed to be Kodachrome or something.”

I expect that the most popular Camera Look will probably be Digi, though in my brief time with the phone I was partial to Minimal. The Digi Look is inspired by digicams, digital cameras from the early aughts that have low dynamic range and high contrast. In just the last five years, search volume for “digicam” is up 500 percent, according to Google Trends, and cameras that used to sell for $5 at thrift stores now go for hundreds of dollars on the secondhand market. Some companies like Canon have even caught wind and are rereleasing old digicam models just to cash in on the trend. It makes sense for Google to want to adopt the look, too.

I’m extremely happy to see Google changing things up in the camera department. At least for me, Google’s Pixel camera processing has gotten far too clinical, and lost the realism that once made it so revered. Now, it’s adapting to what a growing audience says they want from a camera — something real, stylized, and unique to the way they want to see the world.

Photography by David Imel / The Verge

Tech.title: Google’s Pixel Watch 5 dives deeper into AI and health
Tech.content:
The $399 Google Pixel Watch 5 isn’t about the hardware. Sure, there’s a new satin pyrite case finish, a few new strap colors, and a Steph Curry Special Edition. Under the hood, there’s a slightly faster Qualcomm processor and an itty-bitty battery bump. There’s a $50 price hike from last year, too, because the Pixel Watch 5 isn’t immune to RAMageddon — none of us are. Otherwise, no one would blame you for looking at this watch and thinking absolutely nothing’s changed. That’s because the big updates this year are all software-based.

This isn’t a huge surprise considering Google’s Fitbit Air launch in May. And after seeing some Pixel Watch 5 demos, it’s clear this year’s refresh is furthering the AI and proactive health themes that Google introduced earlier this year.

Health and fitness features account for the bulk of the updates, but Gemini on the wrist gets a few key improvements. You can now use it offline for simple tasks like starting timers and launching apps. (Though I noticed in my demo it was notably slower when doing this offline.) Gemini will also be more proactive in making suggestions. One example I saw: a text asking for my availability brought up the option to check Google Calendar from the wrist. Likewise, there’s now an icon right on the watchface that surfaces real-time information for things like timers, Uber ETAs, and workouts. Meanwhile, the pinchy pinch and wrist-flick features came via a software update to Pixel Watches in December, but they’re much more fully integrated into the UI with WearOS 7.

There’s little reason for Pixel Watch 3 or 4 owners to upgrade. Most of the new health software updates will be backward-compatible. Photo: David Imel / The Verge

You can also use AI to generate watchfaces. I created a watchface featuring “fat cats and an elegant font.” It didn’t quite do that. The fat cats weren’t characters, so much as pleasantly plump, cat-shaped clock numbers. It’s a gimmicky way to shoehorn the Nano Banana model onto the watch… but if that’s your thing, it works.

Now for the health stuff. The most novel update is Breathing Emergency Detection. It’s an extension of last year’s Loss of Pulse feature. When the watch detects a severe drop in blood oxygen saturation (aka SpO2), it’ll trigger a call to emergency services and your designated emergency contacts. (A sudden drop in SpO2 may indicate you’re struggling to breathe.) To minimize false positives, the watch uses a combination of heart rate, motion, and altitude sensors. While I didn’t get to see the feature in action, I was told at my demo that the feature won’t kick in unless SpO2 drops to roughly 83 percent — so a significant decrease — for an extended period. It also disables once the watch determines you’ve been asleep for 30 minutes to mitigate false alarms linked to low SpO2 from sleep apnea or side sleeping. The feature also isn’t intended to be used by people with preexisting or chronic respiratory conditions; it’s more for flagging acute instances where a person may have stopped breathing. It’ll be available on both the Pixel Watch 4 and 5 in Europe at launch, and is pending clearance from the FDA in the US.

A less high-stakes feature is that the Pixel Watch (and Fitbit Air) will also track nightly sleep breathing quality and provide monthly updates. The idea is to see how your daily trends impact respiratory health at night over a longer time frame.

Behold, the new satin pyrite case finish and olive strap. Photo: David Imel / The Verge

Two other health features are Blood Pressure Trends and Insulin Resistance Trends. First and foremost: Neither of these is diagnostic. Both are wellness features intended to function as “check engine light”-type warnings, require a minimum of a week’s worth of data, and flag trends monthly. They won’t be available right when the Pixel Watch 5 launches; rollout is currently scheduled for September. That said, these features will also come to the Pixel Watch 3 or later, as well as the Fitbit Air.

With Blood Pressure Trends, the watch will monitor blood flow using the optical heart rate sensor, as well as motion sensors. That data gets fed into an AI model to estimate the shape and speed of pulse waves traveling under the skin to approximate whether your blood pressure is trending higher or lower. (There will be no direct systolic or diastolic measurements.)

While we’ve seen other wearable players like Apple and Whoop tackle blood pressure insights, Google’s attempt at non-invasive insulin resistance detection is brand spanking new. Insulin resistance describes a condition in which your body doesn’t metabolize food effectively. The pancreas has to produce more insulin to utilize blood glucose, and untreated, it often leads to fatigue, stubborn weight gain, and eventually, Type 2 diabetes. This feature would passively estimate whether your insulin resistance is trending higher or lower month to month based on signals like heart rhythm, sleep quality, and daily movements. To validate the algorithm, Google says it tested the algorithm against blood draws and published its findings in a peer-reviewed study in Nature.

Previous Next







1 / 5 This is coming in September to the Pixel Watch 3 and later, plus the Fitbit Air. Photo: Victoria Song / The Verge

Again, this is not noninvasive blood glucose monitoring. As with Blood Pressure Trends, there are no direct readings involved, and this isn’t a screening feature for diabetes. It’s just flagging when your lifestyle trends indicate sustained metabolic stress over a monthlong period. Even so, I’ve spilled a ton of ink on the decadelong process for me to get diagnosed with insulin resistance. It can remain asymptomatic for several years, it may not show up in routine metabolic tests, and a traditional diagnosis involves nagging doctors to test fasting insulin and glucose via blood draws. We’ll have to see how this feature works in real life, but it’s potentially huge if it works well.

That’s health. Google isn’t slacking on the fitness front either. Fitbit and Pixel Watch users have griped for years over dubious GPS maps from outdoor activities, especially in urban areas. Last year, Google introduced dual-frequency GPS. This year, it’s making the bold claim that the Pixel Watch 5 will outperform the Garmin Fenix 8 and Apple Watch Ultra 3 by utilizing satellite and weather station data, as well as 3D models of buildings from Google Maps, to “correct” GPS data using AI in post-processing. Shots fired.

Google is also bringing AI-generated strength training plans to the wrist. This feature is already available with Google Health Premium, but the difference is that you no longer need the phone to log reps or move on to the next exercise. At least based on my demo, this seems like an obvious and smart move given the renewed emphasis on strength training in the GLP-1 era.

It’s all software this year, baby. Plus a $50 price hike. Photo: David Imel / The Verge

All of these health updates are meant to feed into the Google Health app’s AI coach (which requires a Google Health Premium subscription). As I wrote in my Fitbit Air review, Google’s AI coach is the best of the lot — but that is a remarkably low bar at the moment. AI health remains a work in progress, and Google’s coach is no exception — but so far these updates are a savvy mix of potentially helpful and smart for building a long-term AI health roadmap.

The Google Pixel Watch 5 is available for preorder starting today and arrives on shelves August 20th. The Steph Curry Special Edition will hit shelves September 3rd.

Tech.title: Android now has a tap-to-share feature
Tech.content:
is a news writer focused on creative industries, computing, and internet culture. Jess started her career at TechRadar, covering news and hardware reviews.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Android’s AirDrop-like Quick Share feature will now let some devices exchange files and contact information when tapped together. The update is coming to Pixel 6 series phones and newer starting today, according to Google’s announcement, and will roll out to Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, Fold 8, and Flip 8 “soon.”

The tap-to-share feature uses NFC and proximity to simplify sharing, enabling users to wirelessly send contact details, photos, videos, and more by opening the share sheet menu and bringing the two devices close together. Quick Share’s tapping update will also be expanded to “more Android devices by the end of the year,” according to Google, but no device models were specified.

Tech.title: The Pixel Tag is Google’s answer to the AirTag
Tech.content:
More than two years after launching its own device-tracking network, Google has finally followed up with its own tracker. The Pixel Tag, which goes on sale in November, looks like one of the more capable trackers too: It combines ultra wideband (UWB) with Bluetooth 6.0 Channel Sounding for two distinct types of precision tracking.

The Pixel Tag goes on sale on November 11th, unlike the newly announced Pixel 11 and Pixel Watch 5, which are already available to preorder and ship next week. When it arrives, the Tag will cost $29, with a four-pack for $99 — the exact same pricing as Apple’s AirTag 2.

The Pixel Tag is a slim oblong device available in one grayish color — Fog — that weighs about 12g, or 0.4oz. Like the AirTag, it has no built-in hooks or clips for attaching to objects you want to track. There’s a single button that will trigger a sound on your phone, for the rare occasion when you’ve got the Tag but have lost your main device. It also has an IP67 rating, so it should be safe from dust and rain. As for the battery, the Pixel Tag takes CR2032 coin batteries, and says one battery should last for over a year.

It only comes in one color, so I hope you like gray — sorry, Fog.

Naturally, it’ll be compatible with Google’s Find Hub network, which leverages the Bluetooth capabilities of Android devices worldwide to help locate lost objects. After a rocky launch, the network has improved steadily since, though when I tested it last year I found it was still less precise than Apple’s.

Once you’re close enough to the Pixel Tag, UWB lets the Find Hub app display the distance and direction to the tracker, so long as you’re using a phone with a UWB chip. Channel Sounding is a newer development that can display the exact distance, but not direction, and it will work with any phone or tablet that includes Bluetooth 6.0. The Moto Tag 2 is the only other tracker to currently support it.

Google device owners will need a Pixel 10 or later to take advantage of Channel Sounding, and any Pro model since the 6 for UWB — even in the new Pixel 11 series, the base model still lacks UWB. You can track the Tag using a Pixel Watch too, and any model since the 4 will support Channel Sounding, while the 2 or later include UWB. You can also ask Gemini to ring the Tag’s speaker for you.

Tech.title: Jaguar offers a first look inside the all-electric Type 01
Tech.content:
is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Jaguar’s all-electric Type 01 comes with a very beige interior that divides the four seats with a “spine” that spans the length of the cabin. New photos shared by Jaguar show a low-slung driver’s seat, alongside a slim dashboard with a smartphone-style display in the center.

This vehicle doesn’t come with a traditional rear-view mirror, as Jaguar says you’ll find a “ClearSight Rear View Display” at the very bottom of the windshield, positioned at the “same height as the door mirrors, to help the driver focus.” There are also some “concealed compartments” and “hidden‑until‑needed technologies” according to Jaguar, though you can’t make any of that out in the photos.

The Type 01 is a follow-up to the polarizing Type 00 concept Jaguar first revealed in 2024, and is the first production vehicle built on Jaguar’s Electric Architecture. Jaguar will show off the Type 01 prototype under a camo wrap at Monterey Car Week before its official reveal on October 6th.

Tech.title: After Microsoft threatened legal action, a security researcher publishes a new Windows zero-day bug
Tech.content:
A security researcher has published details of a new vulnerability in the latest versions of Windows that allows hackers to gain system-wide access to the user’s device and data, despite facing a legal threat from Microsoft weeks earlier over the release of previously unknown software flaws.

The new bug, dubbed ShieldBreak, is the latest disclosure by security researcher Nightmare Eclipse, who in recent months has published details of several bugs affecting Microsoft’s products, including Windows.

According to Nightmare Eclipse’s post, ShieldBreak takes advantage of a flaw in Windows Defender, the anti-malware and security engine built into Windows. A successful attack allows the hacker to escalate their permissions from a low-level user to full access to the device and its data.

Nightmare Eclipse published the proof-of-concept exploit as a Windows app, requiring the user to run the app to exploit the bug. The bug works on Windows 10, Windows 11 (including the latest 25H2 version), and Windows Server 2025, the researcher said.

Security researcher Will Dormann verified that the bug works and that Windows Defender must be enabled for the exploit to work.

The latest exploit builds on an earlier exploit that Nightmare Eclipse developed dubbed RoguePlanet. Microsoft rolled out a patch for RoguePlanet, but Nightmare Eclipse implied that Microsoft’s fix was not sufficient and that their latest exploit demonstrates a full bypass of the earlier patch.

Microsoft has not yet released a patch for the ShieldBreak bug. A spokesperson for Microsoft did not immediately comment when contacted by TechCrunch. The bug is considered a zero-day because the software maker — in this case, Microsoft — was given no time to patch the bug before it was publicly disclosed.

The release of this new zero-day is the latest in a long back-and-forth between the security researcher and the software giant over the company’s alleged handling of their bug reports.

In a series of blog posts, the security researcher claimed that Microsoft mistreated them and did not handle their bug reports sufficiently, with the implication that the researcher had no other choice but to publicly disclose the bugs online. Nightmare Eclipse previously released several other bugs in Windows that were later exploited in real-world attacks to hack into organizations.

In May, Microsoft published a blog post threatening to take legal action against security researchers, like Nightmare Eclipse, if they released details of zero-days outside of the company’s disclosure policies. The company faced heavy rebuke from the security community, many of whom described similar experiences with Microsoft’s handling of their bug reports. Microsoft later walked back the comments in a social media post. Its original blog post remains published and unchanged.

ShieldBreak lands a day after Microsoft’s regularly scheduled monthly security patch releases, dubbed Patch Tuesday. This is the second month in a row where the number of patches has reached around 500 or so bugs driven by the company’s growing use of AI to find and weed out security flaws.

Tech.title: Silkroad Innovation Hub’s Road to Battlefield competition continues
Tech.content:
The Road to Battlefield competition, organized by Silkroad Innovation Hub in partnership with TechCrunch, Freedom Holding, Astana Hub, IT Park Uzbekistan, is now in its second year. Its purpose hasn’t changed since it launched: Give founders across Central Eurasia a direct route to TechCrunch Startup Battlefield 200 during this year’s Disrupt from October 13 – 15 in San Francisco.

“For two years now, together with our partners, we’ve been organizing Road to TC Startup Battlefield to give founders in our region a direct line to the top VCs and global ecosystems, one they didn’t have before at this scale,” said Asset Abdualiyev, founder and CEO of Silkroad Innovation Hub. “There’s a lot of talent here the world hasn’t found yet, and that’s exactly who we’re looking for, founders and ideas from every corner of the region who haven’t had their moment.”

The program’s first year, 2025, drew 485 applications from 27 countries, the largest startup pitch event the region had seen at the time. Three startups came out of it to represent Central Eurasia on the global stage: Polygraf AI (Azerbaijan/U.S.), Surfaice (Kazakhstan/U.S.), and Investbanq (Singapore/U.S.).

This year, applications jumped to 726 from 39 countries, which is up nearly 50% in submissions and a dozen more countries than last year. This is a record for the program, spanning Central Asia, the Caucasus, the Middle East, Eastern Europe, and South Asia. Founders pitched online in front of 47 judges from eight countries, drawn from top VC firms, major tech hubs, and founders who’ve scaled their own companies, alongside an AI judge, AI-Dana, as independent jury.

What makes the competition worth watching now, in its second year, is its trajectory. Central Eurasia is now producing one of the fastest-growing startup pipelines in emerging markets, and the numbers back it up.

National rounds for Road to Battlefield 2026 ran online from July 6 to 20. Twenty-two startups came out of it, and they’ll now head to a regional final on August 12. From there, judges will narrow the field to three finalists who’ll represent the region at TechCrunch Startup Battlefield 200.

Meet the Road to Battlefield finalists

Those 22 finalists are MoliyAI (Uzbekistan), Sino AI (Uzbekistan), Deepen (Uzbekistan), Fermopolis (Uzbekistan), Oqim App (Uzbekistan), Cerberus (Uzbekistan), Soup (Kazakhstan), CortexAI (Kazakhstan), Scano (Kazakhstan), 4sell.ai (Kazakhstan), WeGlobal AI (Kazakhstan), ZhanCare.AI (Kazakhstan), Kaptın Kaptın (Türkiye), Pocket eSIM (Türkiye), SeaDar (Azerbaijan), Telagri (Georgia), Admyra (U.S.), Soulward (Kyrgyzstan), Suriy (Mongolia), MVSxAI (Qatar), Looq (Japan), and Defensive Pedal (Romania).

Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan each have six startups in the regional final, a clear sign that these two now stand as the region’s largest startup ecosystems.

“We’re seeing steady growth in AI products, especially from Kazakhstan and Central Eurasia, and that tracks exactly with our vision,” said Magzhan Madiyev, CEO of Astana Hub. “This progress reflects the strengthening of our innovation ecosystem and the tremendous work being done across it. At Astana Hub, our mission is to nurture the next generation of globally competitive founders ready to scale into markets like the U.S., and it’s inspiring to see many of them take the stage, compete internationally, and move one step closer to the world’s leading startup stage.”

In fact, AI dominates the applicant pool: 609 of the 726 startups, roughly 84%, are building AI products, underscoring how quickly the technology has become the default starting point for founders in the region.

“For founders from Uzbekistan and across Central Eurasia, entering international markets is becoming part of their strategy from the very beginning, as more startups build products with the potential to compete and scale globally,” said Azamat Karamatov, CEO of IT Park Uzbekistan. “This reflects the region’s shift toward a more connected and competitive innovation ecosystem. For IT Park Uzbekistan, the priority is to strengthen the pathways that connect high potential startups with international investors, customers, expertise, and leading technology ecosystems. Road to TechCrunch Startup Battlefield contributes to this effort by giving founders from our region the opportunity to participate in TechCrunch Disrupt and the Startup Battlefield stage in the U.S., gain global exposure, build valuable international connections, and engage directly with one of the world’s leading technology markets.”

The competition’s youngest applicant is just 14, and 89 of the 726 applicants, including seven founders from Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan, are under 18. Most applicants are early stage, too: 41.6% at MVP and 38.6% pre-seed, with 14.7% at seed and 4.7% still at the idea stage.

Behind the competition is a wide network of regional partners, supported by leading regional innovation hubs and accelerators across Azerbaijan, Bulgaria, China, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova, Mongolia, Qatar, Tajikistan, Türkiye, and Uzbekistan: Accelerate Prosperity, Activat VC, Ardventure, Bilkent Cyberpark, Bilişim Vadisi, Caucasus Ventures, CEVF, Doha Business Consulting, Future Laboratory, Future Unicorns, Global Tech Weekend Tbilisi, Hello Tomorrow Türkiye, IT Park Dushanbe, IT Park Mongolia, Khan Tengri Innovation Hub, MOST, Nazarbayev University, SABAH Angels, SABAH Fund, Silkroad Angels, Sofia Tech Park, Startup Moldova, Stanbase, StartupCentrum, and Terricon Valley, with regional media support from TheTech.

This year brought some new stakes to the table, too:

An $100,000 investment prize pool, split $50,000, $30,000, and $20,000 across the top three finalists, is being funded jointly by Astana Hub Ventures, IT Park Ventures, and Silkroad Innovation Hub.

The top three winners will get up to $100,000 in OpenAI API credits split the same way, while the rest of the Top 22 finalists will each walk away with $10,000 in OpenAI API credits.

“We’ve been supporting the ecosystem from the very beginning, and this year is no exception,” said Marlen Sikhayev, adviser to the president of Freedom Holding Corp. “What stands out most is how much of it is being driven by AI, solutions built right here in Kazakhstan and across our region that are no longer staying local. They’re being shown to the world, on the same stage as the biggest names in tech. That’s exactly what we set out to support when we backed this initiative, and it’s exactly what keeps us backing it.”

The three eventual winners will also get a fully paid trip and accommodation to TechCrunch Startup Battlefield 200 in San Francisco, along with access to a network of more than 1,000 founders spanning 39 countries.

Tech.title: Everything announced at Made by Google ’26: Pixel 11, Pixel Watch 5, Pixel Tag, and tons of Gemini features
Tech.content:
Google is holding its Made by Google 2026 event on Wednesday, unveiling the Pixel 11 series, the Pixel Watch 5, and even a competitor to Apple’s AirTag. The tech giant also used the event to show off new Gemini-powered features across its devices.

Gemini gets more useful on Pixel

Google spent a good portion of the event talking about Gemini and other AI features coming to its devices.

One of the more notable accessibility updates is an expansion of “Live Transcribe” to support American Sign Language. Using the Pixel Camera, users can have sign language translated into text, giving people another way to communicate without relying on typing.

Image Credits:Google

Google also introduced “Rambler,” a new voice-input feature designed to better understand the way people actually talk. Rather than requiring carefully phrased sentences, Rambler is designed to handle run-on sentences, filler words, and less structured speech while still figuring out what the user is trying to say.

There are a few smaller additions, too. “Circle to Search” can now be accessed more directly from the Pixel Camera, allowing users to identify objects, search for things in the distance, translate text, or ask questions about what’s around them without leaving the camera experience.



Pixel 11

Image Credits:Google

The standard Pixel 11 gets a redesigned camera bar that is thinner than the one on the previous generation. Google says the new camera bar is more than 40% thinner and now uses an all-glass surface that stretches across the width of the phone. Google is also increasing the base storage to 256GB, doubling the previous starting capacity.

The starting price for the new model is set at $899, reflecting a $100 increase compared to the Pixel 10. This price hike comes with the decision to drop the 128GB storage option. Plus, the ongoing RAM supply shortage plays a part in this increase.

The Pixel 11 will be available in Frost, Hibiscus, Pistachio, and Obsidian.

Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL

Image Credits:Google

Google is making durability a bigger part of the Pro lineup. The company says the Pixel 11 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro XL have improved drop resistance and a new anti-scratch display coating that provides more than twice the scratch resistance of the Pixel 10 Pro models.

The Pixel 11 Pro starts at $1,099, compared to $999 for the Pixel 10 Pro.

The phones are available in Canyon, Fog, Olive, and Obsidian. Notably, this year’s Obsidian option gets an all-matte finish.

Pixel 11 Pro Fold

Google says the new foldable is nearly 10% lighter and almost 1mm thinner than the Pixel 10 Pro Fold. It also has slimmer bezels, a 48-megapixel main camera, and 30x Super Zoom.

The company is also building on the IP68 water and dust resistance introduced with the Pixel 10 Pro Fold. The Pixel 11 Pro Fold uses a glass-fiber composite back cover designed to better withstand cracking, while a redesigned hinge offers additional protection for the inner display. Google says the changes make the model three times more durable than its predecessor.

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold comes in Olive and Obsidian.

Google takes aim at Apple’s AirTag

Image Credits:Google

Google finally has its own tracking tag. Called Pixel Tag, the small device is designed to help people keep tabs on things such as keys, wallets, and luggage. It connects to Android’s Find Hub network, allowing users to see the tag’s location through the Find Hub app (similar to Apple’s Find My).

The tag, priced at $29 (or $99 for a four-pack), can also be located from a Pixel Watch. Pixel Buds users can ask Gemini to find or ring a Pixel Tag, adding a voice-controlled option for tracking something down.

Pixel Watch 5

Image Credits:Google

The Pixel Watch 5 is getting several health-related updates. The Google Health app will provide monthly summaries of blood pressure trends, with the goal of helping users notice patterns over time. It will also provide monthly summaries of insulin resistance trends.

The 41mm Pixel Watch 5 starts at $399, while the 45mm version starts at $429. Google is also offering a Stephen Curry edition for $579, with an exclusive design built for workouts. (This is featured in the image above.)

Meanwhile, the Pixel Buds Pro is arriving in a new Olive color.

Image Credits:Google

Tech.title: Google’s Quick Share adds a tap-to-share mode
Tech.content:
In Brief

Alongside its Pixel 11 product launches on Wednesday, Google announced it is making fast sharing between its devices easier, with an improved version of Google’s Quick Share feature (similar to Apple’s AirDrop), rolling out now.

The feature will now allow Android users to send their contact information, photos, videos, and more with a tap.

To use the new version of Quick Share, you’ll bring your Android device close to another compatible Android device for what Google calls an “instant, two-way exchange.” Plus, you’ll be able to share photos or videos from the phone’s Share Sheet, then tap devices together to make the exchange.

The addition brings the Pixel lineup more on par with the iPhone, as it follows the launch of the NFC-powered NameDrop feature in Apple’s iOS 17, which similarly allowed iPhone users to share contacts, photos, or videos by touching phones.

The Quick Share update is rolling out starting on Wednesday on Pixel 6 and newer devices, and will soon arrive on the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Fold8, and Flip8 as well. More devices will be supported by year-end, Google says.

Tech.title: Google’s Pixel 11 lineup offers fewer hardware changes, but much more Gemini
Tech.content:
For the last few years, Google’s Pixel has been a showcase of new AI features, with few hardware changes from the previous year’s devices. Similarly, the Pixel 11 series isn’t too different in design and internals from its predecessor.

However, this year’s devices have more Gemini features to complete tasks in the background, including a new Wispr Flow-like transcription feature, a live translation feature that works across content, and a new camera feature that captures the right frames.

Image Credits:Google

AI advances on the Pixel 11

With this year’s Pixel 11 series launch, Google is thinking more agentic AI to complete your tasks. With Gemini, U.S.-based users will be able to order groceries, book rides, or get coffee, for instance. Plus, Gemini can call businesses on users’ behalf for table reservations or appointments. Google said that users can take over or stop tasks at any point in time and also review transcripts for AI-operated calls.

Over the next few weeks, a new slate of connected apps will be able to work with Gemini to get things done, including Granola, Otter.ai, Wix, Fever, Get Your Guide, Localiza, OpenTable (UK), Ticketmaster, iHeartRadio, Pandora, Angi, Thumbtack, and Zocdoc.

The company has also evolved the “Magic Cue” feature from last year to use Gemini, which proactively surfaces contextual information, to now display information from across your apps to help you find suggestions for things like a dinner spot or show.

In May, Google announced a dictation product called Rambler to take on competitors like Wispr Flow and Aqua. Now, that product is making its way to the Pixel phones.

The new Pixel series phones have some other helpful features that might be handy for daily usage, too. First, the device can translate videos, podcasts, and voice messages in the target language. The company is also making its “Circle to Search” gesture-based feature available directly in the camera, something that Apple also did in iOS 27 by making Siri available in the camera.

What’s more, Google is adding an accessibility feature to the camera, which uses Gemini to translate sign language into text to help people communicate with others who have hearing impairments. And the company has redesigned the live transcribe interface for improved communication.

Camera features

Google also added a few AI tricks embedded into its camera. One feature is called “Magic Capture,” which picks the best frames out of hundreds of frames it captures between when users press start and end. The idea is to take a video and get photos as a byproduct. Google said that the feature also auto-crops and unblurs the frames to make them ready for sharing.

The company has upgraded its super zoom from 100x to 120x for Pro phones, and from 20x to 30x for the base Pixel 11. With the new devices, users will be able to create custom looks for the camera, which are specialized filters that appear when users are snapping images.

Image Credits:Google

The Pro phones are also getting faster capture with a feature called “Instant Night Sight,” which takes 4.5x less time than the previous-gen phone’s Night Sight. Google enhanced video shooting, too, with support for 8K resolution with video boost and better stability.

For creators, Google added a “creator suite” mode in video settings, which lets you use Pixel 11 devices as a teleprompter while shooting clips. When you are done shooting, the clip is saved in a dedicated folder, making it easier to find for editing.

Hardware upgrades

All the Pixel phones now run the latest Tensor G6 processor, which has 20% better power efficiency and

allows for 25% faster browsing, as per Google. Plus, it lets users take faster low-light photos with Night Sight Instant.

The new image signal processing on the chip also enables 120x magic zoom on the Pixel 11 Pro XL. The company said that the new processors run the latest models with lower latency, but didn’t offer any specific metrics.

The display size on all phones is the same, but the Pro models get a slightly brighter display, which could be helpful in the daylight.

Image Credits:Google

Google said Pro models get an updated main camera sensor that takes higher-quality photos than the previous generation without specifying any numbers. It also said the new telephoto sensor allows for 32% more light while capturing an image.

Image Credits:Google

London-based startup Nothing made its phones recognizable by Glyph bars and then a Glyph interface. Google is not that extravagant, but it has now placed an LED light on the back, which is built around the flashlight. This acts as an indicator for calls or messages from favorite contacts when Gemini is thinking or listening.

All these devices are available to pre-order starting today and will start with a base storage of 256GB.

The Pixel 11 starts at $899, the 11 Pro starts at $1,099, and the 11 Pro XL starts at $1,299. (The prices of the Pixel 11 and the Pixel 11 Pro are the same as last year’s 256GB models, but you could buy a 128 GB model at that time with a $100 lower price tag.)

With the rising prices of components, the company has bumped the price of the top model by $100 compared to the Pixel 10 XL.

A new lineup of Pixel 11 accessories is also arriving alongside the phones, including new Pixelsnap cases (which now include clear) and Pixelsnap Ring Stand colors.

Tech.title: Google unveils the Pixel Watch 5 with a smarter Gemini and advanced health monitoring
Tech.content:
At its Made by Google event on Wednesday, Google unveiled the Pixel Watch 5 with a smarter Gemini experience, as well as advanced fitness and health monitoring. The new smartwatch, which starts at $399, can track blood pressure patterns and insulin resistance, as well as deliver personalized help and better sleep tracking.

Google says it’s designed the watch to deliver personalized and proactive help right when it’s needed. For example, the watch will proactively suggest relevant actions or information based on a text message’s context, like instantly pulling up a smoothie place your sister sent you.

You can raise your wrist to ask Gemini a question, handle requests like finding a nearby lunch spot with navigation, or use Gemini offline to manage timers, alarms, and workouts with your voice.

The watch will also dynamically surface timely updates right at the bottom of the watch face, like flight info, ETAs, and other helpful reminders.

Image Credits:Google

The Pixel Watch 5 is also launching with “Health Guardian,” a suite of new proactive health and safety tools.

The tech giant says the smartwatch uses sensors and machine learning to track blood pressure patterns before they can put strain on your heart. Google says the feature was tested against 24-hour blood pressure monitors and uses an advanced waveform model trained on more than 1 billion minutes of data from over 500,000 people.

The insulin resistance feature is designed to identify changes in metabolic health that may be associated with insulin resistance and an increased risk of developing prediabetes or type 2 diabetes. The feature combines signals from sleep, heart rate, physical activity, and other health data. A large sensor model then analyzes these signals over time to identify long-term changes in insulin resistance.

Google will give users a summary of their blood pressure and insulin resistance trends every month.

There’s also a new feature that can detect a persistent drop in oxygen saturation and will contact emergency services if the watch determines that a breathing emergency may be occurring. This feature is launching in select European countries before expanding to additional regions.

Image Credits:Google

Additionally, the watch’s sleep-stage tracking is 15% more accurate, and there’s also a new bedtime watch face that reduces nighttime distractions. A new “Smart Wake” feature wakes users at an optimal point in their sleep cycle, while a new sleep breathing quality metric tracks minute-by-minute changes in blood oxygen levels.

As for fitness, Google says the Pixel Watch 5 delivers its most accurate GPS route tracking yet, with route mapping that’s two times more accurate than previous generations. The improved accuracy is designed to provide users with more precise workout and running data, including a closer match between your recorded route and the actual course.

The Pixel Watch 5 features the Qualcomm Snapdragon W5 Gen 2 platform and has 12% more CPU performance and 50% more RAM than the previous platform. Google says the Watch 5 is 20% faster overall.

The Pixel Watch five supports up to 40 hours of battery life and is available in new colors, including Canyon Fog and Olive. The 41mm version starts at $399, while the 44mm starts at $429. The smartwatch is available for pre-order starting Wednesday and will be available on August 20.

Tech.title: Google takes on AirTag with the new $29 Pixel Tag
Tech.content:
Alongside its announcement of a new lineup of Pixel 11 smartphones, Google on Wednesday introduced its answer to Apple’s AirTag. At its Made by Google ’26 event, the company unveiled a new product designed for keeping track of your valuable items: the $29 Google Pixel Tag.

Similar to how Apple’s AirTag leverages its network of iPhones to find lost devices, the new Pixel Tag uses Google’s Find Hub network, which taps into Android devices around the world. Android users can add the tag to their phone’s built-in Android Find Hub, which is already used to help users find their lost Android smartphones and other devices, similar to Apple’s Find My.

Helpfully, you can locate and ring your Pixel Tag directly from your Pixel Watch, too, not just your phone.

Image Credits:Google

Where the Pixel Tag differs from AirTag is in its look and feel.

Apple’s lost-item finder is small, round, and engravable; Google opted for a slimmer, elongated device instead. Spec-by-spec, the Pixel Tag is 1.1 inches wide, compared to the AirTag’s 1.26 inches. As the Pixel Tag is oval-shaped, it’s 1.8 inches high from top to bottom. Thickness-wise, the Pixel Tag clocks in at a depth of 0.2 inches, compared with the AirTag’s 0.31 inches (which Apple calls its height).

By weight, the two competitors are comparable, as the Pixel Tag weighs 0.4 ounces with the battery, and the AirTag comes in at 0.39 oz.

Both are also rated IP67 for splash, water, and dust resistance, meaning they can withstand submersion in a maximum depth of 1 meter for up to 30 minutes.

Image Credits:Google

Taking other cues from AirTag, the Pixel Tag offers connectivity via Bluetooth and Ultra Wideband for precision finding; however, it doesn’t include NFC. Pixel Tag has a built-in speaker to help you find the lost device when nearby, and it’s powered by the user-replaceable CR2032 coin cell battery — the same used by the AirTag. This allows the Pixel Tag to work for roughly a year before the battery needs to be replaced.

Designed to be attached to items like keychains and bags, the Pixel Tag will cost $29 for a one-pack and $99 for a four-pack when it becomes available for purchase on November 11, 2026.

Tech.title: Google’s new Pixel 11 Pro Fold offers a stronger build and brighter screens
Tech.content:
Samsung’s short and wide foldable is the talk of the town, but Google is not experimenting with its design with today’s unveiling of the new Pixel 11 Fold, which appears largely unchanged on the outside. The company said that the new foldable is stronger and lighter than the previous-gen phone, but it’s also costlier.

Google said that it developed a new, stronger hinge for this year’s Pixel 11 Pro Fold. It’s also adding a Super Actua display to the outer display with 3,600 nits of peak brightness. Both the inner and outer displays are 20% brighter than its predecessor, according to the company.

There is a bit of a battery downgrade, however, as it now offers a 4,750 mAh capacity battery instead of 5,015 mAh from last year’s model. On the plus side, this is probably the reason why the phone is 1mm thinner and roughly 20 grams lighter.

Image Credits:Google

Another small upgrade on the charging front is that the new foldable supports 25W wireless charging.

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is getting an updated 48-megapixel sensor that pulls in more light for more detailed photos in different lighting conditions. Because of the new G6 Tensor chip and the updated image processor, the phone can digitally zoom at 30x, up from 20x.

The device will be available in both the Olive and Obsidian colors, and will cost $1,899.

Tech.title: Google’s Pixel Watch 5 Can Now Detect Breathing Emergencies
Tech.content:
Google's first smartwatch debuted just four years ago, and at the time, the company went to great lengths to stress the accuracy of the Pixel Watch's heart rate sensor. Even if Google was late to the wearable party compared to peers like Apple and Samsung, that focus on heart rate seems to be paying off with new features that are yet to be seen on competing products.

On Wednesday, Google introduced the latest generation of its smartwatch, the Pixel Watch 5 (alongside the Pixel 11 smartphone family). The hot new health feature? Breathing Emergency Detection. Similar to the first-of-its-kind Loss of Pulse Detection feature introduced on the Pixel Watch 3, this new capability can be triggered by a variety of factors, like drug toxicity, accidents, severe pneumonia, and choking.

“Using a combination of data from the advanced sensors, including a PPG, accelerometer, and barometer, we've designed an AI-based algorithm running on device to detect a persistent drop in oxygen saturation and then call Emergency Services for you and even share your location,” says Francis Hoe, a product manager on Google's Pixel Watch team.

This feature hasn't been cleared by the Food and Drug Administration, which is why it's not launching in the US at the moment; Google says it's working with regulators to expand availability. It will only be available in select markets in the European Union to start. Google also says it's not intended for people with preexisting respiratory conditions and isn't designed to diagnose or treat medical conditions.

Courtesy of Google

You also don't need a new Pixel Watch 5 to take advantage; Google's bringing this feature to the Pixel Watch 4 as well. And two other big new capabilities are also coming to older devices: blood pressure and insulin resistance trends. These are coming to the Google Health app and will be available for anyone with a Fitbit Air, Pixel Watch 3, Watch 4, or Watch 5 later this fall.

“It might have felt strange—why are we harping about heart rate accuracy so much—back then,” Sandeep Waraich, senior director of Wearables at Google, tells WIRED. “We kept investing in that, and now it's very improved, because all these large sensor models can detect these signatures, insulin resistance, blood pressure trends—but underneath, they need a really capable raw signal.”

Google is placing these features into a new umbrella category called Health Guardian, which includes existing features such as irregular rhythm notifications, high/low heart rate notifications, Loss of Pulse, and Sleep Breathing Quality. The idea is to put these capabilities in a place where users can easily see what they have turned on, similar to Google's Personal Safety app on Pixel phones, which shows features like Emergency SOS, Safety Check, and Car Crash Detection in one place.

Tech.title: 4 New Camera Tricks on Google’s Latest Pixel 11 Smartphones
Tech.content:
The new Pixel 11 Pro, announced today, can zoom up to 120X, though in addition to the digital stitching, it relies on AI-generated pixels to fill in some details. Reynolds says maybe having that capability is enough to get someone interested in, say, wildlife photography. After experimenting on their phone, they’d be ready to invest in a professional camera and a big zoom lens.
